accordion.name: Accordion
accordion.summary: Stacked headings that each reveal a section, with single or multiple open items.
accordion.description: Use Accordion to shorten long pages whose sections people read selectively, such as FAQs, settings groups and policy details. Avoid hiding content everyone needs. Built on the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern with real headings and buttons.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when items open or close.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Single mode: allow closing the open item.

accessibility: Each trigger is a button inside a heading, with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Each panel is a region labelled by its trigger.
Arrow keys, Home and End move between headers; disabled items are skipped.
Closed panels are removed from the accessibility tree.

keyboard.description: Opens or closes the focused section.
Moves to the next or previous header.
Moves to the first or last header.
Moves through headers and into open panels.

do: Write triggers as clear questions or section names.
dont: Nest accordions.
Hide critical information in a closed panel.

action-menu.name: ActionMenu
action-menu.summary: A compact “more actions” menu built from an array, ideal for table rows and cards.
action-menu.description: ActionMenu is a convenience over DropdownMenu for the common overflow pattern: an icon button that reveals row-level or card-level actions. Describe the actions as data (labels, icons, shortcuts, separators, groups and submenus) and it renders an accessible menu. Use DropdownMenu directly when you need checkable items or custom content.

examples.name: InARow
examples.title: In a table row
examples.description: Give each trigger a unique label so screen-reader users know which row it acts on.

props.name: items
props.description: Actions: `{ label, onSelect, icon, shortcut, destructive, disabled, items }`, `{ type: "separator" }` or `{ type: "group", label, items }`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label of the default trigger. Make it specific in lists.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Replace the default icon button (rendered with asChild).

accessibility: The default trigger is an IconButton with an accessible name; pass a row-specific label such as “Actions for Ben Hughes”.
Inherits the complete DropdownMenu keyboard model: arrows, Home/End, typeahead, submenus and Escape.
Focus returns to the trigger after an action is chosen.

keyboard.description: Open and focus the first action.
Move between actions.
Run the focused action.
Close without acting.

do: Show the primary row action inline and put the rest in the ActionMenu.
Put destructive actions last, after a separator.
dont: Hide the only way to perform an important action inside an overflow menu.

ai-generated-label.name: AIGeneratedLabel
ai-generated-label.summary: A small label that marks content as generated, assisted or edited by AI, with an optional model name.
ai-generated-label.description: Use AIGeneratedLabel wherever AI content sits beside content written by people: a drafted reply, a summary on a record, an edited paragraph. It says what happened in words, next to the sparkle icon, so readers always know what they are looking at.

examples.name: WithModel
examples.title: With the model name
examples.description: model is added in words after the label.

props.name: variant
props.description: How AI took part in the content.

props.name: label
props.description: Overrides the words for this variant.

props.name: model
props.description: The name of the model, added after the label.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations for the three variants and the template that joins label and model.

accessibility: The label is plain text, so screen readers read it in place with the content it marks.
The sparkle icon is decorative; the words carry the meaning.
It uses muted ink that meets contrast in every theme, and system colours in forced colours mode.

do: Place it close to the content it describes, in the same position every time.
Choose the variant that is true: generated, assisted or edited.
dont: Rely on the sparkle icon alone to mark AI content.
Label content a person has fully rewritten as generated.

alert-dialog.name: AlertDialog
alert-dialog.summary: An interruptive dialog that asks the user to confirm or cancel an important action.
alert-dialog.description: AlertDialog is for decisions with consequences, such as deleting a template or revoking access. Unlike Dialog it cannot be dismissed by clicking outside, it has no close icon, and focus starts on the least destructive option. For the common confirm/cancel case with async handling, use ConfirmationDialog.

examples.name: WithDetails
examples.title: With details
examples.description: Use the body for consequences the user should weigh.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render your own Button as the trigger.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: Override the default focus on AlertDialogCancel.

props.name: onEscapeKeyDown
props.description: Call preventDefault() to block Escape (e.g. while saving).

props.name: asChild
props.description: Confirms and closes. Call event.preventDefault() in onClick to keep it open.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Cancels and closes; receives initial focus.

accessibility: Uses role="alertdialog" with aria-modal, named by the title and described by the description.
Initial focus is on Cancel so an accidental Enter never triggers the destructive action.
Outside clicks do not dismiss; Escape cancels.
Focus is trapped and returns to the trigger on close.

keyboard.description: Moves between Cancel and the action.
Activates the focused button.
Cancels and closes.

do: Phrase the title as a question naming the object: “Delete ‘Sales signature’?”
Label the action with the verb, not “OK”.
dont: Use for information-only messages.
Stack alert dialogs or show them on page load.

alert.name: Alert
alert.summary: An inline message about the state of a page or section, in four tones.
alert.description: Alert sits in the content flow, near what it describes, and stays until the situation changes or the user dismisses it. Use it for form-level errors, expiring connections or plan limits. For page-wide announcements use Banner; for transient confirmations use Toast.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replace the tone icon or hide it.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons or links under the message.

props.name: role
props.description: Override the automatic role (alert for warning/danger, status otherwise).

accessibility: Warning and danger alerts use role="alert" and are announced immediately; info and success use role="status".
Tone is conveyed by icon and title text, never colour alone.
Status colours meet 4.5:1 contrast in all three themes; high contrast adds heavier borders.

do: Say what happened and what to do next.
Place the alert next to the content it concerns.
dont: Render role="alert" messages on page load for non-urgent information.
Stack several alerts; combine them.

aspect-ratio.name: AspectRatio
aspect-ratio.summary: Holds images, video and embeds to a fixed width-to-height ratio so layouts never shift.
aspect-ratio.description: AspectRatio reserves space for images, video and embeds before they load, so the layout does not shift. Its single child fills the box; images and video default to object-fit: cover.
accessibility: AspectRatio adds no semantics. Give the media inside it a text alternative.

do: Use for any media whose size is known in advance.
dont: Put text content inside; it may be clipped.

attachment-tray.name: AttachmentTray
attachment-tray.summary: The files and images attached to a draft or a sent message, with upload progress, errors and a remove button on each.
attachment-tray.description: Use AttachmentTray in the header of PromptComposer while people prepare a message, and again inside the sent message in read only form. It only shows state: your app uploads the files and passes progress and errors in.

examples.name: Uploading
examples.title: Progress and errors
examples.description: progress runs from 0 to 1. An error replaces the progress bar and is announced once.

props.name: items
props.description: The attachments: { id, name, kind, size?, previewUrl?, progress?, error? }. An empty list renders nothing.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Called with the id of the attachment to remove. Without it there are no remove buttons.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Show the attachments of a sent message, with no remove buttons.

props.name: formatSize
props.description: Formats a size in bytes. The default gives “12 KB” or “1.4 MB”.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations: list, remove(name), uploading(name) and failed(name, error).

accessibility: A list with an accessible name, so screen readers announce how many attachments there are.
Each remove button is named after its file, for example “Remove contract.pdf”.
Upload progress is a progressbar named for the file, with the percentage as its value text.
A failed upload is shown as text beside an icon, never by colour alone, and is announced politely once when it happens.
After a file is removed, focus moves to the next remove button, so keyboard users keep their place.
Thumbnails are decorative: the file name beside them carries the meaning.

keyboard.description: Moves between remove buttons.
Removes the focused attachment.

do: Say why an upload failed and what to do about it.
Show the same tray, read only, on the sent message.
dont: Hide a failed file; keep it with its error until it is removed.
Use it to pick files; pair it with an attach button or FileUpload.

avatar-group.name: AvatarGroup
avatar-group.summary: A stack of overlapping avatars with a "+N" overflow, announced as a list.
avatar-group.description: Use AvatarGroup to show who is involved, such as template editors, contract signers or team members, in limited space. Set max to collapse extra people into a counter, and total when the full list is not loaded.

props.name: total
props.description: Total count when it exceeds the children provided.

props.name: size
props.description: Overflow counter and overlap size; match your avatars.

accessibility: Rendered as a <ul>, so screen readers announce the number of people. Name it with aria-label.
The overflow counter is announced as "3 more" (customisable) rather than "+3".
Each avatar keeps its own accessible name.

do: Pair the group with a link to the full list when people need details.
dont: Show more than about five avatars before collapsing.

avatar.name: Avatar
avatar.summary: A person or organisation shown as an image or initials, with optional presence.
avatar.description: Avatar shows who something belongs to. Without an image, or if it fails to load, it shows initials on a tint taken from the name, so a person keeps the same colour everywhere. Tints are mixes of ivory and indigo, so they stay within the Binds palette in every theme.

examples.name: Shapes
examples.title: Organisations
examples.description: Use the square shape for organisations and workspaces.

props.name: name
props.description: Used for initials, tint and the accessible name.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL; falls back to initials while loading or on error.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Announced status text; defaults to the status name.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Hide from assistive tech when the name is already visible.

accessibility: Exposed as role="img" named after the person, including status, e.g. "Ada Lovelace (online)".
The inner image has an empty alt, so the name is not announced twice.
Set decorative when the name appears as text next to the avatar.
Presence is announced in text; the coloured dot is visual reinforcement only.

do: Show the person’s name next to small avatars.
dont: Use avatars as the only way to identify people in dense lists.

badge.name: Badge
badge.summary: A short, non-interactive status or count label in six tones and three variants.
badge.description: Use Badge to label status ("Deployed", "Pending") or counts. Tones are functional: success, warning, danger and info carry meaning, while neutral and inverse are for categorisation. Use Tag for removable keywords and Chip for selectable filters.

props.name: tone
props.description: Meaning conveyed by colour; always pair with text.

props.name: count
props.description: Numeric count when there are no children.

accessibility: Badges are static text. The tone is never the only signal; the label text carries the meaning.
Give count-only badges context with aria-label, e.g. aria-label="12 unread notifications".
Every tone and variant meets 4.5:1 text contrast in light, dark and high-contrast themes.

do: Keep labels to one or two words.
Use the same tone for the same status everywhere.
dont: Make badges clickable; use Chip or Button.
Rely on tone without text.

banner.name: Banner
banner.summary: A full-width, page-level announcement such as maintenance windows or plan limits.
banner.description: Banner spans the top of the page or app shell and applies to the whole product, not one section. The default brand tone uses inverse ivory and indigo; status tones communicate urgency. Show at most one banner at a time and let people dismiss non-critical ones.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.title: Controlled dismissal
examples.description: Persist dismissal yourself, e.g. in user settings.

props.name: action
props.description: A link or button after the message.

props.name: icon
props.description: Custom or hidden icon (status tones show one by default).

accessibility: Rendered as a labelled <section> region so it can be found from the landmarks list.
It is not a live region: content present on load is read in order. For urgent changes after load, use Alert or Toast.
The dismiss button has an explicit accessible name.

do: Keep the message to one sentence with one action.
Remember dismissal across sessions.
dont: Use banners for marketing on every page.
Show several banners at once.

box.name: Box
box.summary: The lowest-level layout primitive: padding, surface, border, radius and shadow from tokens.
box.description: Box renders any element with spacing and surface styles taken directly from Stance tokens. Use it to build one-off containers without writing CSS. When a pattern repeats, such as a card or a panel, prefer the dedicated component, which carries semantics and states.

examples.name: Surfaces
examples.title: Surfaces
examples.description: Each background sets a matching foreground, so text stays legible in every theme.

examples.name: Semantic
examples.title: Semantic element
examples.description: Use `as` to render a landmark or list item while keeping the styling.

props.name: padding
props.description: Padding on all sides from the space scale.

props.name: paddingX
props.description: Horizontal padding; overrides padding on the x axis.

props.name: paddingY
props.description: Vertical padding; overrides padding on the y axis.

props.name: background
props.description: Semantic surface with a matching foreground.

props.name: shadow
props.description: Elevation token. Becomes an outline in high contrast.

accessibility: Box has no role of its own. Choose a semantic element with `as` (section, aside, li) when the content has structure.
The inverse background flips foreground colour automatically, so contrast is preserved without extra props.

do: Use Box for one-off spacing and surfaces.
Pick backgrounds by meaning (surface, subtle), not by colour.
dont: Rebuild Card, Alert or Banner with Box; use the component.
Override token colours with inline styles.

branch-switcher.name: BranchSwitcher
branch-switcher.summary: Steps between alternative versions of a message after an edit or a retry, and shows which one is on screen.
branch-switcher.description: When a message is edited or an answer is regenerated, keep the earlier versions and let people move between them with BranchSwitcher. It shows the position, for example 2 of 3, and reports the new index. It renders nothing when there is only one version.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.title: Switching the answer
examples.description: The index is zero based.

props.name: count
props.description: How many versions exist. Nothing renders for fewer than two.

props.name: index
props.description: Controlled, zero based index of the version on screen.

props.name: defaultIndex
props.description: Initial index when uncontrolled. Default: the last version.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Called with the new zero based index.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable both buttons, for example while a response streams.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations: group, previous, next, and position as a function of index and count.

accessibility: A labelled group with Previous version and Next version buttons.
The position text is a polite live region, so a change is read as 2 of 3.
At the first and last version the button is marked disabled but keeps focus, so keyboard users do not lose their place.
The arrows mirror in right to left layouts.

keyboard.description: Moves between the two buttons.
Shows the previous or next version.

do: Place it beside the message actions of the message it belongs to.
dont: Use it for paging through unrelated content; use Pagination.

breadcrumbs.name: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.summary: Shows where the current page sits in a hierarchy and links back up it.
breadcrumbs.description: Use Breadcrumbs on pages that are two or more levels deep, such as a template inside a team inside an organisation. They complement, not replace, primary navigation. Long trails collapse their middle items behind an expandable ellipsis, and on screens narrower than 640px they collapse to the first and last items.

examples.name: Collapsed
examples.title: Collapsed trail
examples.description: More items than maxItems collapse behind an ellipsis button that reveals them and moves focus to the first revealed link.

examples.name: WithRouterLinks
examples.title: With router links
examples.description: Use asChild to render your framework link component, such as Next.js Link.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark.

props.name: separator
props.description: Content between items; always hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: maxItems
props.description: Collapse middle items when there are more items than this.

props.name: collapseOnMobile
props.description: Below 640px, show only the first and last items.

props.name: expandLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the ellipsis button.

props.name: href
props.description: Destination. Items without href render as text.

props.name: current
props.description: Marks the current page with aria-current="page" and renders plain text.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render your own link element with breadcrumb styles.

accessibility: Renders a <nav> landmark with an accessible name and an ordered list, so screen readers announce the number of levels.
The current page is plain text with aria-current="page"; it is not a link to itself.
Separators are aria-hidden, so they are not read as “greater than” or similar.
The ellipsis is a real button announcing how many items are hidden; after expanding, focus moves to the first revealed link.

keyboard.description: Moves between links and the expand button.
Follows a link or expands the collapsed items.

do: Use the page title as the last item.
Keep labels short; long labels truncate at 16rem.
dont: Use breadcrumbs for linear flows; use Stepper.
Show breadcrumbs on top-level pages where there is nothing above.

button-group.name: ButtonGroup
button-group.summary: Groups related buttons, either joined into a segmented bar or evenly spaced.
button-group.description: Use ButtonGroup to show that several actions belong together, such as export formats or pagination steps. Attached groups read as one control; spaced groups simply align actions like dialog footers. For buttons that hold an on/off state, use ToggleButtonGroup instead.

props.name: variant
props.description: Join buttons or keep a gap between them.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Buttons share the full container width.

accessibility: Renders role="group"; provide label so screen readers announce what the buttons relate to.
Each button remains its own tab stop. For a single tab stop with arrow keys, use Toolbar or ToggleButtonGroup.

keyboard.description: Moves between the buttons in the group.

do: Keep attached groups to between two and five actions of equal importance.
dont: Mix primary and outline buttons in one attached group.

button.name: Button
button.summary: Triggers an action, with six variants, four sizes and a loading state.
button.description: Use Button for actions that change something: saving, submitting, opening a dialog. Use Link for navigation that only moves the user elsewhere. Keep one primary button per view so the main action is unambiguous.

examples.name: Variants
examples.title: Variants
examples.description: Emphasis from strongest to weakest. Danger is reserved for destructive actions.

examples.name: Sizes
examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: Control heights of 24, 32, 40 and 48px align with inputs of the same size.

examples.name: Loading
examples.title: Loading
examples.description: Loading keeps the button focusable and announces aria-busy while blocking repeat clicks.

examples.name: Pill
examples.title: Pill shape
examples.description: Fully rounded ends for marketing calls to action.

examples.name: AsLink
examples.title: As a link
examples.description: Use asChild to give a router link button styling while keeping link semantics.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner, sets aria-busy and blocks clicks.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the child element with button styles.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All native button attributes. type defaults to "button".

accessibility: Renders a native <button>, so it is focusable and activates with Enter and Space without extra code.
type defaults to "button" to prevent accidental form submission; pass type="submit" explicitly.
Icon-only actions should use IconButton, which requires an accessible label.
Loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled but keeps focus, so keyboard users do not lose their place.
Focus is shown with a 2px ring (3px in high contrast) offset from the button edge.

keyboard.description: Activates the button.
Activates the button.

do: Start labels with a verb: “Save changes”, “Invite member”.
Use one primary button per view.
dont: Use a button to navigate between pages; use Link.
Disable a submit button to signal errors; show the errors instead.

calendar.name: Calendar
calendar.summary: A keyboard-accessible month grid for choosing a date or a date range.
calendar.description: Calendar is the always-visible date grid used inside DatePicker and DateRangePicker. Use it directly when a date choice is the main task of the view, such as scheduling a signature roll-out. Dates outside min/max or rejected by isDateDisabled cannot be selected. Month and weekday names come from Intl, so it follows the chosen locale with no date library.

examples.name: Range
examples.title: Range, two months
examples.description: Click a start and end date; hovering previews the range.

examples.name: Constraints
examples.title: Min, max and disabled dates
examples.description: Only weekdays in the next three weeks are available.

examples.name: Localised
examples.title: Locale and week start
examples.description: US English with weeks starting on Sunday.

props.name: mode
props.description: Select one date or a range.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new date or range.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for names and labels.

props.name: captionLayout
props.description: Dropdown shows month and year menus so people can jump to a distant date. Label shows a plain title.

props.name: fromYear / toYear
props.description: First and last year in the year menu. Default to the min and max years, or 100 years back and 10 ahead.

props.name: today
props.description: Override today, e.g. for a time zone or tests.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focus the active day on mount.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translatable strings for navigation and day states.

accessibility: Month and year menus are native selects with accessible names, so they work with every keyboard, screen reader and touch device.
Each month is a grid labelled by its month and year; weekday headers carry full names via abbr.
Each day is a button with a full spoken label, e.g. “Wednesday, 11 November 2026, Today, Selected”; today has aria-current="date".
Unavailable days stay discoverable but are announced as unavailable and cannot be chosen.
The month title is a polite live region, so changing months by keyboard is announced.
One day is in the Tab order; arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Home/End follow the APG date grid model.

keyboard.description: Previous / next day.
Same day previous / next week.
First / last day of the week.
Same day previous / next month.
Same day previous / next year.
Select the focused day (start, then end in range mode).

do: Set min and max whenever dates outside a window are invalid.
Use the user’s locale.
dont: Use a calendar for dates far in the past, like birth dates; let people type instead (DatePicker).

caption.name: Caption
caption.summary: Small supporting text for figures, timestamps and footnotes.
caption.description: Caption is 12px secondary text. Use it with `as="figcaption"` under figures, and for timestamps, footnotes and legal small print. For text that helps someone fill in a form field, use the description of FormField, which is linked to the control.
accessibility: Muted captions meet 4.5:1 contrast in every theme.
Use figcaption so the caption is associated with its figure.

do: Keep captions to one or two lines.
dont: Put essential instructions in captions.

card.name: Card
card.summary: A contained surface for related content, with header, media, content and footer parts.
card.description: Use Card to group information about one subject, such as a template, contract or integration. Cards can be static, contain actions, or be fully clickable through CardLink. Avoid nesting cards inside cards.

examples.name: Interactive
examples.title: Clickable card
examples.description: CardLink stretches its hit area across the card. Header actions stay clickable above it.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Make the card a click target through its CardLink.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render as the child element, e.g. <article>.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Aspect ratio of the media area.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render your router link as the card link.

accessibility: CardTitle renders a real heading; choose a level that fits the page outline.
Clickable cards use one real link (CardLink) rather than onClick on a div. Its accessible name is the title, so screen-reader link lists stay concise.
Buttons and links in an interactive card are lifted above the stretched link, so they stay independently operable.
The focus ring is drawn around the whole card while its link has keyboard focus.

keyboard.description: Moves to the card link, then to any actions in the card.

do: Keep one primary action per card.
Use asChild with <article> for self-contained content.
dont: Wrap a whole card in <a> when it contains buttons.
Nest cards.

chart-container.name: ChartContainer
chart-container.summary: An accessible chart frame with title, legend, responsive sizing and a data-table alternative.
chart-container.description: ChartContainer is not a charting engine. It gives any chart a consistent frame: a title and description, a legend using the theme-aware chart colours, the measured width for responsive drawing, and a “View as table” toggle so the data is never locked inside graphics. Stance includes two small SVG charts built on it: BarChart and Sparkline.

examples.name: Custom
examples.title: Custom chart
examples.description: Use the render function to draw your own SVG with the measured size and series colours.

examples.name: Sparklines
examples.title: Sparkline
examples.description: Word-sized trends for stat cards and tables, with a generated text summary.

props.name: description
props.description: What the chart shows; linked with aria-describedby.

props.name: series
props.description: { key, label, color? } per series. Colours default to --st-color-chart-1…5.

props.name: data
props.description: Rows for the data table alternative.

props.name: categoryKey
props.description: Key of the category column in data.

props.name: children
props.description: The chart, or a render function receiving the measured size.

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Defaults to true when there are series.

props.name: actions
props.description: Extra header controls, such as a period selector.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: Fixed axis maximum; defaults to a rounded data maximum.

props.name: label
props.description: Overrides the generated summary; null hides it when adjacent text describes the trend.

accessibility: The container is a <figure> named by its title and described by its description.
BarChart and Sparkline render role="img" with a generated summary, such as “Highest: Deployed in Sep, 260”.
“View as table” replaces the chart with a real data table, the most reliable way for screen reader users to explore values.
Chart colours come from the ink ramp and adapt to each theme. Pair colour with labels; never rely on colour alone.

keyboard.description: Toggles between chart and table views.

do: Write a title that states the insight, not just the metric.
Always provide data for the table alternative.
dont: Use more than five series in one chart.
Use charts where a single number in a StatCard would do.

checkbox-group.name: CheckboxGroup
checkbox-group.summary: A labelled set of checkboxes that share one array value.
checkbox-group.description: Use CheckboxGroup when users can choose any number of options from a short list. It renders a fieldset and legend, so the group label is announced with each option, and manages the selected values as a string array. For more than about eight options, consider MultiSelect.

props.name: label
props.description: Group label, rendered as the legend.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name applied to every checkbox.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message; marks every checkbox invalid.

props.name: required
props.description: Shows a required indicator on the legend.

accessibility: Uses <fieldset> and <legend>, so the group name is announced when focus enters the group.
Description and error are linked to the fieldset; the error uses role="alert".
Each checkbox remains a separate tab stop, matching native behaviour.

keyboard.description: Moves between checkboxes.
Toggles the focused checkbox.

checkbox.name: Checkbox
checkbox.summary: A native checkbox with label, description and an indeterminate state.
checkbox.description: Use Checkbox for independent yes/no choices that are applied on submit, such as accepting terms or opting into notifications. Use Switch for settings that take effect immediately, and CheckboxGroup for several related options under one label.

examples.name: Indeterminate
examples.title: Indeterminate (select all)
examples.description: The parent reflects a partial selection of its children.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Without it, provide aria-label.

props.name: description
props.description: Help text under the label, linked via aria-describedby.

props.name: value
props.description: Form value; identifies the item inside a CheckboxGroup.

props.name: ...props
props.description: Native input attributes; the ref targets the <input>.

accessibility: A real <input type="checkbox"> is styled, so native semantics, form submission and keyboard behaviour are preserved.
The indeterminate state is set on the element and exposed as "mixed".

The checkmark is drawn in the accent foreground colour and remains visible in Windows forced colours.

dont: Use a checkbox for an action that happens immediately; use Switch.

chip.name: Chip
chip.summary: A selectable toggle chip for quick filters and choices.
chip.description: Use Chip for lightweight on/off choices, such as quick filters above a list. Each chip is a toggle button that reports its state with aria-pressed. For filters with a value to edit, use FilterChip; for removable labels, use Tag.

examples.name: QuickFilters
examples.title: Quick filters
examples.description: A controlled set of chips filtering a list.

Selection is shown by fill, a check mark and aria-pressed, not by colour alone.
Group related chips with role="group" and an aria-label.

keyboard.description: Toggles the chip.

do: Use short, parallel labels.
Label the group, e.g. "Status filters".
dont: Use chips for mutually exclusive choices; use RadioGroup or ToggleButton.

citation-chip.name: CitationChip
citation-chip.summary: An inline numbered marker that links a claim to its source and previews it on hover, focus or tap.
citation-chip.description: Place a CitationChip right after the sentence it supports. Readers can check the source without leaving the answer: the preview shows the title, site and snippet, and activating the marker opens the source.

Keyboard focus opens the preview and links it to the marker as its description. Escape closes it and focus stays on the marker.

The marker stays small in text while its hit area meets the minimum target size.

Number sources in the order they first appear.

code-block.name: CodeBlock
code-block.summary: A multi-line code sample with title, line numbers, highlighting and copy.
code-block.description: CodeBlock shows source code with light, dependency-free highlighting for TypeScript, CSS, shell and JSON. Code is always rendered as text, never as HTML. The scroll region is focusable so keyboard users can scroll long lines.

Highlighting never carries meaning on its own.

Scroll the focused code region.

do: Keep samples short and runnable.
dont: Render user-supplied HTML as code output.

code.name: Code
code.summary: Inline code for identifiers, values and file names in running text.
code.description: Use Code for short fragments inside a sentence. For multi-line samples use CodeBlock, and for one line the reader should copy use CopyableCode.

props.description: With or without a background chip.

Long values wrap anywhere instead of overflowing.

do: Use for literal values the reader might type.
dont: Use for emphasis.

collapsible.name: Collapsible
collapsible.summary: A single disclosure: one trigger shows and hides one region.
collapsible.description: Collapsible is the primitive behind progressive disclosure, such as "Advanced settings", "Show details" or long log output. It is unstyled apart from focus, so you compose the trigger, often with Button asChild. Use Accordion for a group of related disclosures.

dont: Use for navigation menus; use NavigationMenu.

combobox.name: Combobox
combobox.summary: An editable input with a filtered list of suggestions, supporting async search and custom values.
combobox.description: Use Combobox when the list is long enough that people need to type to find an option, such as assigning a template to one of hundreds of organisation users. It filters as you type, can search a server (filter={false} with a controlled input), and can accept free text with allowCustomValue. For short fixed lists use Select.

Use descriptions to tell similar options apart, such as email addresses.
dont: Use Combobox for short lists where Select is faster.
Allow custom values when only listed values are valid.

command-menu.name: CommandMenu
command-menu.summary: A searchable, keyboard-driven list of commands with groups, keywords and shortcuts.
command-menu.description: CommandMenu combines a search field with a filtered list of actions. It is the building block for CommandPalette and can also be embedded inline, for example in an empty state or a sidebar quick-switcher. Filtering uses a built-in fuzzy scorer over each item’s value and keywords; pass your own scorer or disable filtering for server-side search.

Focus stays in the input; arrow keys move the highlight, so typing is never interrupted.
Groups are role="group" named by their heading; separators are hidden from assistive technology.
The empty message lives in a polite status region.

Jump to the first or last item.
Run the highlighted command.

Add keywords for synonyms people actually type.
dont: Put more than ~50 items in one group without search hints.

command-palette.name: CommandPalette
command-palette.summary: A global ⌘K / Ctrl+K command menu in a dialog for fast navigation and actions.
command-palette.description: CommandPalette puts a CommandMenu in a modal dialog that opens from anywhere with a keyboard shortcut. Use it to give power users one place to jump between pages and run common actions. Mount one per app. The examples on this page use hotkey={false} (except the last) so they do not clash with the docs search on ⌘K.

props.description: Optional button that opens the palette.

props.name: label
props.description: Dialog title (visually hidden) and input label.

All CommandMenu keyboard behaviour applies inside.
The shortcut is discoverable through the trigger button and the footer hint; never make the hotkey the only way in.

keyboard.description: Toggle the palette (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux).
Move through results.

Close.

do: Show the shortcut on a visible trigger, e.g. “Search ⌘K”.
Group results by type: pages, actions, people.
dont: Register several palettes on one page with the same hotkey.

confidence-badge.name: ConfidenceBadge
confidence-badge.summary: States how sure the system is about an answer in plain words, with a distinct icon for each level.
confidence-badge.description: Use ConfidenceBadge when your product has a real signal for how reliable an answer is, such as source agreement or a verification step. It says the level in words and gives each level its own icon shape, so the meaning never depends on colour. Leave it out when there is no signal behind it.

examples.description: description appears on hover and keyboard focus, and is read to screen readers.

accessibility: The level is always written out. Icons are decorative and differ by shape, so the badge reads the same without colour.
It uses the neutral ink scale only; no red, amber or green.
With a description the badge can be focused, and the explanation is linked to it as its accessible description.
Without a description it is plain text and adds no tab stop.

Hides the explanation.

do: Explain what the level is based on in the description.
Use unknown when there is no signal, instead of guessing.
dont: Show a level your product cannot justify.
Use it as decoration on every message.

confirmation-dialog.name: ConfirmationDialog
confirmation-dialog.summary: A ready-made confirm/cancel dialog with async loading and error handling, plus an imperative useConfirm() hook.
confirmation-dialog.description: ConfirmationDialog wraps AlertDialog with the props most confirmations need. When onConfirm returns a Promise, the confirm button shows a spinner, Cancel and Escape are blocked, the dialog closes on success and shows the error message on failure. ConfirmProvider and useConfirm() give you `await confirm({...})` from any event handler, which replaces window.confirm and hand-rolled confirm contexts.

Errors from a rejected promise are shown in a role="alert" message inside the dialog.

Throw an Error with a human message from onConfirm on failure.
dont: Ask for confirmation of easily undone actions; offer Undo in a toast instead.

container.name: Container
container.summary: Centres page content with a maximum width and responsive gutters.
container.description: Container sets the readable width of a page region. Sizes come from the size tokens: sm 640, md 880, lg 1240 (the Binds site width) and xl 1440. The side gutters scale from 16 to 40px with the viewport.

Use lg for marketing pages and dashboards.
dont: Nest containers; one per region.

context-chips.name: ContextChips
context-chips.summary: Chips that show what the assistant can see for a message, such as files, pages or selections, each one removable.
context-chips.description: Use ContextChips above the composer so people always know what will be sent with their message, and can take things out. This is a matter of trust as much as layout: nothing should be shared with the assistant that is not shown here.

Each remove button is named after its item, for example “Remove pricing.md”.
The “+N more” button exposes aria-expanded and keeps focus when it reveals or hides items.
After an item is removed, focus moves to the next remove button, or to the add button when none are left.

Use names people recognise: the file name, the page title.
dont: Include context that is not shown as a chip.
Use chips for uploads in progress; use AttachmentTray.

context-menu.name: ContextMenu
context-menu.summary: A menu that opens at the pointer on right-click, long-press, Shift+F10 or the Menu key.
context-menu.description: Use ContextMenu for shortcuts to actions on a specific object, such as a block in the signature editor or a row in a document list. Every action in a context menu must also be reachable another way (a toolbar or ActionMenu), because context menus are hard to discover. conversation-list.name: ConversationList
conversation-list.summary: A list of past conversations grouped by date, with selection, inline rename, delete and pin.
conversation-list.description: Use ConversationList in a sidebar so people can return to earlier conversations. Items are grouped under Pinned, Today, Yesterday and older ranges, or under your own group names. The list reports what people do; your app owns the data.

copy-button.name: CopyButton
copy-button.summary: Copies text to the clipboard and confirms it visually and to screen readers.

copyable-code.name: CopyableCode
copyable-code.summary: One line of code with a copy button, for commands, keys and IDs.
copyable-code.description: CopyableCode suits installation commands, API endpoints and identifiers. An optional prompt such as `$` is shown but not copied. Long values scroll horizontally instead of wrapping.

data-grid.name: DataGrid
data-grid.summary: A spreadsheet-style grid with cell navigation, in-place editing, resizable columns and virtualised rows.
data-grid.description: Use DataGrid when people work inside the data: bulk-editing signature fields for hundreds of mailboxes, or reviewing large imports. It implements the WAI-ARIA grid pattern with a single tab stop and arrow-key navigation, and only renders visible rows. For read-mostly collections with sorting and selection, use DataTable.

Committed and cancelled edits are announced in a polite live region.

description-list.name: DescriptionList
description-list.summary: Key to value pairs such as account details or contract metadata, using native <dl>.
description-list.description: Use DescriptionList to show attributes of one thing: an organisation’s settings, a contract’s parties and dates, an integration’s configuration. Choose horizontal for detail pages, vertical for narrow panels and grid for summary headers. Every layout stacks on phones.

Show "None" for empty values rather than omitting the row.
dont: Use for comparisons across many items; use Table.

dialog.name: Dialog
dialog.summary: A modal window for focused tasks that must be finished or dismissed before returning to the page.
dialog.description: Use Dialog for short, self-contained tasks such as renaming a template or inviting a colleague. It traps focus, locks page scroll and returns focus to the trigger when closed. For confirming destructive actions use AlertDialog; for long or secondary content use Drawer; for non-blocking content use Popover. On phones the dialog becomes a bottom sheet automatically.

Keep dialogs short; move long flows to a page or Drawer.

disclaimer-note.name: DisclaimerNote
disclaimer-note.summary: A quiet note under the composer or a response, such as a reminder to check important facts.
disclaimer-note.description: Use DisclaimerNote for standing information about how the assistant works: answers can be wrong, conversations may be reviewed, a feature is in preview. It is calm by design and is not announced on its own. For something the reader must act on now, use Alert or Banner.

It is not a live region and is never announced while a response streams.
The icon is decorative. The text uses muted ink that still meets contrast in every theme.
An action keeps its own name and focus ring, and gains a 24px target on touch screens.

do: Keep it to one or two short sentences.
Say what the reader should do, for example check important facts.
dont: Use it for errors or anything urgent.
Repeat it under every message; once near the composer is enough.

divider.name: Divider
divider.summary: Separates sections of content, optionally with a short label such as “or”.
divider.description: Divider marks a change of topic between sections. It renders a native thematic break (<hr>), or a labelled separator when it carries text. Inside menus and toolbars, use the lighter Separator.
accessibility: Unlabelled dividers are <hr> elements, announced as separators.
Labelled dividers use role="separator" and expose their text.
Lines become CanvasText in Windows forced-colours mode.

do: Use between distinct sections.
dont: Use a divider under every heading; whitespace usually suffices.

drawer.name: Drawer
drawer.summary: A modal panel that slides in from a screen edge for details, filters and secondary tasks.
drawer.description: Drawer keeps the page in context while showing longer content than a Dialog comfortably holds, such as a user’s profile or a filter panel. It shares Dialog’s behaviour: focus trap, scroll lock, Escape to close and focus return. Side panels never exceed the viewport width on phones.

examples.description: Slide from any edge. Use left for navigation, right for details.

Respects prefers-reduced-motion: the slide animation is removed.

Closes the drawer.

do: Use for detail views that benefit from keeping the list visible behind.
Put persistent actions in DrawerFooter.
dont: Use as primary app navigation on desktop; use Sidebar.

dropdown-menu.name: DropdownMenu
dropdown-menu.summary: A menu of actions or options opened from a button, with groups, checkable items and submenus.
dropdown-menu.description: Use DropdownMenu for a set of actions that apply to the current context, such as everything you can do with a signature template. For choosing a value in a form, use Select; for site navigation, use NavigationMenu. DropdownMenu implements the WAI-ARIA menu pattern with roving focus, typeahead and submenus, and has no third-party dependencies.

High contrast mode adds a visible focus ring to the highlighted item; Windows forced colours use the system Highlight.

Keep labels short and verb-first: “Duplicate”, “Assign to users”.

empty-state.name: EmptyState
empty-state.summary: Explains why an area is empty and offers the next step.
empty-state.description: Use EmptyState for first-run screens, empty search results and cleared filters. Say what would normally be here, why it is empty, and give one clear action. Keep the tone helpful and brief.

The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
When results empty out after filtering, pair this with a live results count (see FilterBar) so the change is announced.

do: Offer the action that fills the space.
For no results, suggest clearing filters.
dont: Blame the user or use jokes in error-adjacent states.

error-boundary.name: ErrorBoundary
error-boundary.summary: Catches rendering errors in part of the screen and shows a recoverable fallback.
error-boundary.description: Wrap independent regions, such as a signature preview, a chart or an integration panel, so a failure in one does not blank the whole page. The default fallback is an accessible alert with a retry button; you can supply your own. ErrorBoundary catches rendering errors only. Handle event and async errors where they happen.

examples.description: Changing resetKeys clears the error, e.g. when the user opens another template.

accessibility: The default fallback uses role="alert", so the failure is announced when it appears.
Technical details are in a collapsed disclosure, so they do not overwhelm the message.
The retry button is a native button. After a reset, the region renders again in place.
Write fallback copy that says what failed and what the person can do next.

keyboard.description: Activates the retry button in the default fallback.

do: Wrap independent regions separately so the rest of the screen keeps working.
Send errors to monitoring with onError.
dont: Wrap the entire app in a single boundary only.
Show raw stack traces to end users.

feedback-bar.name: FeedbackBar
feedback-bar.summary: Thumbs up or down on a response, followed by optional reasons and a comment, then a thank you.
feedback-bar.description: Use FeedbackBar when you want more than a rating: the reason a response was good or bad. A rating opens a short, optional detail step. For a rating alone inside a row of message actions, use MessageActions. FeedbackBar holds no data itself; you receive the result in onSubmit.

Reasons are toggle chips in a group labelled by its visible question; the comment field has a visible label.
The thank you is announced politely, once, and focus returns to the rating instead of being lost.
Every step works with the keyboard, and rating buttons and chips grow to 44px on touch screens.
The current step is exposed as data-state: idle, rated, detail or submitted.

On Send feedback: submits.

Keep the detail step optional; Skip still records the rating.
dont: Require a comment before a rating counts.
Show both FeedbackBar and rating buttons in MessageActions on the same message.

file-tree.name: FileTree
file-tree.summary: A TreeView preset for folders and files, with open and closed folder icons.
file-tree.description: Use FileTree to browse uploaded assets, exported templates or any folder structure. It is a TreeView with folder and file icons chosen by extension, so it shares the same keyboard model, selection and props. Pass getFileIcon to customise file icons.

Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

Show full file names, including extensions.
dont: Use FileTree for non-file hierarchies; use TreeView.

file-upload.name: FileUpload
file-upload.summary: Choose files by browsing or drag and drop, with type, size and count validation.
file-upload.description: Use FileUpload to attach documents, logos or spreadsheets. It validates against accept, maxSize and maxFiles before files reach your code, lists accepted files with remove buttons and reports rejected files clearly. Upload progress belongs to your own logic: render it with Progress beside the list, or set hideFileList and render your own.

Rejected files are listed in a role="alert" region with specific reasons; additions and removals are announced in a polite live region.
Each remove button is labelled with the file name ("Remove contract.pdf").

Moves through the browse button and remove buttons.

Keep files visible after selection so people can verify them.
dont: Rely on drag and drop alone.
Start uploading silently without showing progress.

filter-bar.name: FilterBar
filter-bar.summary: A responsive row of search, filters, results count and "Clear all".
filter-bar.description: FilterBar assembles the filtering controls above a table or list: an optional search field, any number of FilterChips, a "Clear all" action and a results count that screen readers hear when it changes. It wraps on narrow screens without breaking the page.

The results count is a polite live region (role="status"), so screen readers announce new totals without moving focus.
The search field is a native search input with an accessible label.
Hide "Clear all" with canClear={false} when nothing is active, so it is not a dead control.

dont: Announce counts on every keystroke for slow searches; debounce first.

filter-chip.name: FilterChip
filter-chip.summary: A filter control showing its name and current value, editable in a popover.
filter-chip.description: FilterChip packs a filter into one compact control. When inactive it reads "+ Status". When active it shows the selected value and a clear button. Put any editor you like inside the popover, such as checkboxes, a date range or a search list. Combine several in a FilterBar.

The popover is a labelled dialog ("Status filter") that returns focus to the trigger on close.
The clear button is a separate button labelled "Clear Status filter", never nested inside the trigger.
Inactive filters use a dashed border plus a plus icon, so state is not shown by colour alone.

Closes the editor and returns focus.

dont: Apply changes on every keystroke when results are slow; add an Apply button.

floating-action-button.name: FloatingActionButton
floating-action-button.summary: The primary action of a screen, floating above content in a corner.
floating-action-button.description: Use FloatingActionButton on touch-first or content-heavy screens where the main action must stay reachable while scrolling, such as creating a new signature from a long list. Use at most one per view. On desktop dashboards a regular primary Button in the page header is usually clearer.

props.name: extended

props.description: Fixed viewport corner, or static to place it yourself.

Fixed positioning respects device safe areas so the button is never hidden by the home indicator.
Place the FAB late in the DOM so its tab position matches its visual prominence without jumping ahead of content.

keyboard.description: Activates the action.

do: Use for a single, positive, frequent action (create, compose).
dont: Use for destructive or secondary actions.
Show more than one FAB on a screen.

form-field.name: FormField
form-field.summary: Wires a label, help text and error message to any Stance form control.

generation-progress.name: GenerationProgress
generation-progress.summary: Progress for longer generations such as images or documents, with a stage label and a way to cancel.
generation-progress.description: Use GenerationProgress when making something takes more than a few seconds: an image, a report, a long export. Give it a value when you can measure the work, and leave the value out when you cannot. Name the current stage so people know it is moving. For a short wait before text use ThinkingIndicator.

grid.name: Grid
grid.summary: Two-dimensional layout with fixed columns that collapse responsively, or fluid auto-fit tracks.
grid.description: Use Grid for dashboards, galleries and card collections. Fixed `columns` collapse to two columns on tablets and one on phones. `minChildWidth` instead fits as many columns as there is room for, which suits galleries of unknown size.

Keep related cells adjacent in source order.
dont: Use Grid to lay out data that has row/column relationships; use Table.

heading.name: Heading
heading.summary: Section headings with a semantic level and an independent visual size.
heading.description: Choose `level` to match the document outline and `size` to match the visual hierarchy. Keeping them separate lets a card title be an h3 that looks small, or a hero be an h1 at display size, without breaking the outline screen-reader users navigate by.

Display and 3xl sizes scale fluidly with clamp() and respect browser zoom.

do: Write headings that describe the content below.
Use sentence case.
dont: Pick a level for its size; use size.

hover-card.name: HoverCard
hover-card.summary: A rich preview that appears when hovering or focusing a link.
hover-card.description: HoverCard lets sighted users peek at a person, template or document without leaving the page. It is purely supplementary: the link must lead somewhere that shows the same information, because touch and screen reader users will not see the card. For content users must interact with, use Popover.

examples.name: Delays
examples.title: Custom delays
examples.description: Shorter delays suit dense lists; longer ones avoid accidental opens.

Keep the card to a summary: name, role, a few facts.
