icon-button.name: IconButton
icon-button.summary: A compact button that shows only an icon and always carries an accessible label.
icon-button.description: Use IconButton for frequent, well-understood actions where space is tight: close, copy, more options, row actions in tables. The label prop is required and becomes both the accessible name and the native tooltip. If the meaning of the icon is not obvious, use a Button with text instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name; also used as the title tooltip.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon to show, usually <Icon name="…" />.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner and blocks clicks.

props.name: hideTitle
props.description: Drop the native title when wrapped in a Tooltip.

accessibility: label is required by the type system, so icon-only buttons can never ship without an accessible name.
The icon is aria-hidden; the label is announced instead.
Use the xs size only inside dense layouts with enough spacing to meet the 24px minimum target (WCAG 2.5.8).

keyboard.description: Activates the button.
Activates the button.

do: Use universally understood icons: close, search, copy, more.
Pair with a Tooltip for richer hints.
dont: Use an icon-only button for a primary, uncommon action.

icon-gallery.name: IconGallery
icon-gallery.summary: A searchable grid of every Stance icon; choose one to copy its name.
icon-gallery.description: IconGallery lists the Stance icon set with live search. By default choosing an icon copies its name for use with <Icon name="…" />. Pass onSelect to build an icon picker, for example when choosing an icon for a navigation item.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Replace copy with a custom action.

accessibility: The search field is labelled, and the result count is announced as you type.
Each icon is a button named after its action, e.g. “Copy icon name check”.
Copy confirmation is announced in a live region.

keyboard.description: Moves through the search field and icons.
Copies or selects the focused icon.

icon.name: Icon
icon.summary: Original Stance icons as inline SVG that inherit the current text colour.
icon.description: Stance ships its own icon set, drawn on a 24px grid with a 1.75 stroke and round joins, with no icon-library dependency. Icons are decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology. Give an icon a `label` only when it stands alone and carries meaning.

examples.name: Meaningful
examples.title: Meaningful icons
examples.description: A standalone status icon needs a label.

props.name: name
props.description: Icon identifier. See the Icons page for all names.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name; omit for decorative icons.

accessibility: Without a label, icons get aria-hidden="true" and focusable="false".
With a label, icons get role="img", aria-label and a <title>.
Icons use currentColor, so they follow text colour in all themes and in forced-colours mode.

do: Pair icons with text for actions.
Use the same icon for the same concept everywhere.
dont: Use an icon alone without a label.

image.name: Image
image.summary: An image with lazy loading, a reserved ratio and a graceful fallback.
image.description: Image wraps with lazy loading, asynchronous decoding, rounded corners from tokens and an optional ratio that stops layout shift. When the source fails to load it shows a neutral placeholder that keeps the alt text available to assistive technology.

examples.name: Fallback
examples.title: Fallback
examples.description: A broken source shows a placeholder.

props.name: alt
props.description: Text alternative; empty for decorative images.

accessibility: alt is required by the type. Pass alt="" for decorative images.
Fallbacks keep the alt text via role="img".

do: Describe what the image conveys, not what it looks like.
dont: Embed text in images.

inline-edit.name: InlineEdit
inline-edit.summary: Text that can be edited in place: activate it to type, press Enter to save or Escape to cancel.
inline-edit.description: Use InlineEdit for a single value people change now and then where they read it: a template name, a document title, a short note. For several related fields, or values that need explanation, use a form with FormField instead.

examples.name: WithValidation
examples.title: Validation
examples.description: validate returns an error message to reject a value. The editor stays open so it can be fixed.

examples.name: WithActions
examples.title: Confirm and cancel buttons
examples.description: With showActions, leaving the field no longer saves; people choose explicitly.

examples.name: Multiline
examples.title: Multiline
examples.description: Enter adds a line and Ctrl/⌘+Enter saves.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being edited, e.g. "template name". Names the read view “Edit <label>” and the input.

props.name: onCommit
props.description: Called with the new value when it changes and is saved.

props.name: validate
props.description: Return an error message to reject the value and keep editing.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the read view when the value is empty.

props.name: showActions
props.description: Show Save and Cancel buttons while editing.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size, to match the surrounding content.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shows the value as a disabled button.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the value as plain text with no edit affordance.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations for the Save and Cancel buttons.

accessibility: The read view is a real button named “Edit <label>: <value>”, so it is reachable by keyboard and announces what activating it does.
Entering edit mode moves focus to the input and selects the text; saving or cancelling returns focus to the read view.
Validation errors are linked to the input and announced immediately, and the editor stays open.
The pencil icon appears on hover and focus, and is always visible on touch screens where there is no hover.
With showActions, Save and Cancel are labelled buttons that stay inside the editor’s focus area.

keyboard.description: On the read view: starts editing.
While editing: saves. In multiline mode it adds a line.
In multiline mode: saves.
Cancels and restores the previous value.
Leaves the field, saving the value (unless showActions is on).

do: Use a specific label: “template name”, not “value”.
Use showActions when a change has consequences people should confirm.
dont: Use it for several fields that are saved together; use a form.
Rely on it for required information that has no value yet; ask for it in a form.

inline.name: Inline
inline.summary: Lays children out horizontally and wraps them, for tags, actions and metadata.
inline.description: Inline is a horizontal Stack that wraps by default and centres its items. Use it for groups that should reflow onto new lines on small screens: filters, tag lists, toolbars of buttons and metadata rows.
accessibility: Visual wrapping does not change reading order.
Use `as="ul"` for lists of tags so their count is announced.

do: Use for content that may wrap on small screens.
dont: Use for vertical rhythm; use Stack.

input.name: Input
input.summary: A single-line text field with sizes, affixes and validation states.
input.description: Use Input for short free-text values: names, emails, URLs, reference numbers. Wrap it in FormField to get a label, help text and error message wired up automatically. For multi-line text use Textarea; for numbers with steppers use NumberInput.

examples.name: Sizes
examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: Heights match Button sizes so controls line up in toolbars.

examples.name: Affixes
examples.title: Prefix and suffix
examples.description: Static text or icons inside the field box.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid. Set automatically inside a FormField with an error.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Content before the text, inside the field box.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Content after the text, inside the field box.

props.name: wrapperClassName
props.description: Class for the outer box; className goes to the <input>.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All native input attributes; the ref targets the <input>.

accessibility: Always give the input a visible label via FormField, or aria-label when a visible label is genuinely redundant.
Inside FormField the input receives id, aria-describedby (description and error), aria-invalid, required and disabled automatically.
Placeholders are hints, not labels: they disappear on input and have lower contrast.
Focus is shown by a solid ring on the whole field box, including in high contrast mode.
Use the correct type and autoComplete (email, tel, url) to get the right mobile keyboard and autofill.

keyboard.description: Moves focus to and from the input.

do: Size the field to the expected length of the value.
Explain format requirements in the description, before the user makes a mistake.
dont: Use placeholder text as the only label.
Disable paste on email or password fields.

interrupted-state.name: InterruptedState
interrupted-state.summary: Marks a response that was stopped or failed part way, and offers to try again or continue.
interrupted-state.description: Place InterruptedState directly under a response that did not finish, so it is clear the text above is incomplete and what can be done about it. Keep what was already written. Use the reason to tell a stop the reader chose apart from a failure.

examples.name: Reasons
examples.title: Reasons
examples.description: Errors and lost connections are alerts. A stop or a limit is a quiet status.

props.name: title
props.description: Overrides the default title for the reason.

props.name: description
props.description: A short explanation or next step.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Shows a retry button and is called when it is pressed.

props.name: onContinue
props.description: Shows a continue button and is called when it is pressed.

props.name: children
props.description: Extra actions, shown after the buttons.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations: the default titles stopped, error, network and limit, and the buttons retry and continue.

accessibility: Errors and lost connections are an alert and are announced at once. A stop or a limit is a polite status.
Only the message is live. The buttons are not read out with it.
The reason is given in words and with an icon, never by colour alone.
Retry and Continue are real buttons with visible labels.

keyboard.description: Moves between Continue, Try again and any extra actions.
Activates the focused button.

do: Keep the partial response on screen above it.
Say what happened and what to do next in plain words.
dont: Use the error reason when the reader pressed stop.
Offer Continue when the response cannot be picked up where it ended.

kbd.name: Kbd
kbd.summary: Displays a keyboard key or shortcut with spoken labels for symbols.
kbd.description: Kbd shows a single key, or a shortcut given as `keys`. Modifier names such as mod, shift and alt render as symbols, and each symbol also carries a text label, so screen readers say “Command plus K” rather than reading the glyph.

props.name: children
props.description: A single key when keys is omitted.

accessibility: Uses nested <kbd> elements, the HTML idiom for key combinations.
Symbols are aria-hidden and paired with visually hidden names.

do: Show the platform-appropriate modifier.
dont: Use Kbd for non-keyboard input.

label.name: Label
label.summary: A form label with required and optional indicators.
label.description: Label names a form control. In most forms, use FormField, which renders the label and wires up ids, descriptions and errors for you. Use Label directly for custom controls or layouts that FormField does not cover.
accessibility: Always connect the label with htmlFor, or let FormField do it.
The asterisk is aria-hidden; screen readers hear “(required)” instead.

do: Mark whichever is rarer, required or optional.
dont: Use placeholder text instead of a label.

link.name: Link
link.summary: Navigates to another page or resource, inline in text or on its own.
link.description: Use Link for navigation and Button for actions. Inline links are underlined so they can be told apart without colour. External links open in a new tab, carry rel="noopener noreferrer", and tell screen-reader users that a new tab will open. Use `asChild` to style your router’s link component.

examples.name: RouterLink
examples.title: With a router
examples.description: Pass your framework’s link as the child, e.g. Next.js <Link>.

props.name: external
props.description: Open in a new tab with icon and announcement. Defaults to true when target="_blank".

accessibility: Inline links are underlined, so they are distinguishable without colour (WCAG 1.4.1).
External links announce ", opens in a new tab" and include rel="noopener noreferrer".
Focus shows a 2px outline offset from the text.

keyboard.description: Follows the link.

do: Write link text that makes sense out of context.
dont: Use “click here”.
Use a link to perform an action; use Button.

list-item.name: ListItem
list-item.summary: A list row with leading media, title, description, metadata and actions.
list-item.description: ListItem lays out one row of a List. Pass structured props for the common layout, or children for custom content. With asChild, the main area becomes your link or button while actions stay separate, so each row has one clear primary target.

examples.name: Interactive
examples.title: Interactive rows
examples.description: asChild makes the main area a real link or button. Actions sit outside it.

props.name: meta
props.description: Trailing metadata such as a date or badge.

props.name: actions
props.description: Trailing actions, outside the interactive area.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the main area as your single link or button child.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dim the row and disable pointer interaction.

accessibility: Renders an <li>, so it must be inside a List (or another <ul>/<ol>).
With asChild, the whole main area is one link or button whose accessible name combines the title and description.
Actions render after the main area, so tab order is: row, then its actions.
selected sets aria-current="true" for navigation-style lists.

keyboard.description: Moves to the row’s link or button, then to its actions.
Follows the row link or activates the row button.

do: Give interactive rows a single primary destination.
dont: Put buttons inside an asChild link; use actions instead.

list.name: List
list.summary: A semantic list of related items with dividers, density and an optional bordered surface.
list.description: Use List for collections people scan top to bottom, such as members, templates or recent activity. Each row is a ListItem. Use Table instead when people need to compare values across columns.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Wrap the list in a bordered surface.

props.name: ...props
props.description: Native list attributes; use aria-label to name the list.

accessibility: Renders native <ul> or <ol>, so screen readers announce the number of items.
Name lists that stand alone with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
Keep interactive items to one primary target per row (see ListItem asChild) so tab order stays predictable.

do: Keep titles short and put secondary detail in the description.
Use ordered lists when sequence matters.
dont: Nest interactive elements inside an interactive row.
Use List for tabular comparisons.

loading-overlay.name: LoadingOverlay
loading-overlay.summary: Covers a region or the whole screen with a spinner while work is in progress.
loading-overlay.description: LoadingOverlay keeps layout stable while content refreshes, and prevents interaction with stale data. The covered content is marked aria-busy and made inert so it cannot be clicked or focused. Prefer Skeleton for first loads and a Button’s loading state for single actions; use the overlay when a whole panel is temporarily unusable.

examples.name: Solid
examples.title: Solid backdrop
examples.description: Hide content entirely when partial data would mislead.

examples.name: FullScreen
examples.title: Full screen
examples.description: For app-wide transitions such as switching organisation.

props.name: message
props.description: Shown under the spinner and announced politely.

props.name: fullScreen
props.description: Cover the viewport (rendered in a portal).

props.name: children
props.description: Content to cover; made inert and aria-busy while visible.

accessibility: The wrapper has aria-busy="true" while visible and the content is inert (not focusable or clickable).
The message is in a role="status" region so screen readers hear it once.
The spinner slows instead of stopping under prefers-reduced-motion.

do: Write a specific message: “Deploying signatures…”.
Return focus to a sensible place when loading finishes.
dont: Cover the screen for background refreshes; update in place instead.

mention-picker.name: MentionPicker
mention-picker.summary: A filterable list that opens from a trigger character in the composer, to reference files, people or tools by name.
mention-picker.description: Open MentionPicker when someone types a trigger character such as @ in PromptComposer. Focus stays in the text area while arrow keys move through the list. The picker does not parse the draft: your app decides when it opens, passes the query, and inserts the chosen item.

examples.name: InComposer
examples.title: Mention with @
examples.description: Type @ to open the list, keep typing to filter, then press Enter.

examples.name: LoadingAndEmpty
examples.title: Loading and no matches
examples.description: With filter off the app supplies results, for example from a search request.

props.name: items
props.description: What can be referenced: { id, label, description?, icon?, group? }.

props.name: anchor
props.description: The focused element the list belongs to, normally the composer text area. The list is placed against it and reads keys from it.

props.name: query
props.description: The text typed after the trigger character.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen entry. Insert it or run it, then close the list.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with false on Escape or a press outside.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows the loading label instead of the entries.

props.name: filter
props.description: Filter by query on the name and description. Set false when the server filters.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the listbox, for aria-controls on the text area.

props.name: onActiveDescendantChange
props.description: Called with the id of the active option, for aria-activedescendant on the text area.

props.name: disablePortal
props.description: Render in place instead of in a portal.

accessibility: A listbox with an accessible name. Focus never leaves the text area, so typing continues without interruption.
Point the text area at the list with aria-controls and aria-activedescendant, using id and onActiveDescendantChange. Screen readers then read each option as it becomes active.
The active option is marked with aria-selected and a visible highlight, with an added outline in high contrast and forced colours.
Escape closes only the list. The draft and the caret stay as they were.
Loading and empty states are a polite status, so they are announced without moving focus.
Options are at least 32 pixels tall, and 44 pixels on touch screens.

keyboard.description: Move the active option, wrapping at the ends.
Move to the first or last option.
Choose the active option.
Closes the list and keeps the draft.

do: Open it as soon as the trigger character is typed and filter with every keystroke.
Add a description when names alone are ambiguous, such as a file path.
dont: Move focus into the list; people are in the middle of typing.
Use it for commands; use SlashCommandMenu.

menubar.name: Menubar
menubar.summary: A persistent bar of menus for editor-style applications, as in File, Edit and View.
menubar.description: Use Menubar in dense, application-like tools such as a signature template editor, where users expect desktop-style menus. It implements the WAI-ARIA menubar pattern: one tab stop for the whole bar, arrow keys between menus, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to move between open menus. For website navigation use NavigationMenu instead.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: Control which menu is open with value / onValueChange.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: The open menu’s value (controlled or initial).

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when a menu opens or closes.

props.name: loop
props.description: Wrap focus between first and last menus.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name of the menubar, e.g. “Template editor”.

props.name: value
props.description: Identifier for controlled usage. Generated by default.

props.name: align / sideOffset
props.description: Placement of the menu under its trigger.

accessibility: The bar has role menubar and a single tab stop (roving tabindex) across its triggers.
Triggers are menuitems with aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls.
With a menu open, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight close it and open the neighbouring menu with focus on its first item.
Hovering across the bar while a menu is open switches menus, matching desktop conventions.

keyboard.description: Move between triggers, or between open menus.
First or last trigger.
Open the menu and focus its first item.
Open the menu and focus its last item.
Close the menu and return focus to its trigger.

do: Reserve for application-like editors with many commands.
Show keyboard shortcuts for frequent commands.
dont: Use for marketing or documentation site navigation.

message-actions.name: MessageActions
message-actions.summary: The row of actions under a message: copy, try again, edit, good response and bad response, plus any of your own.
message-actions.description: Place MessageActions in the actions slot of a Message. Each button appears only when you pass its handler. The component reports what was pressed; storing ratings and regenerating answers stays in your app.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.title: Controlled rating
examples.description: Pressing the active rating clears it.

examples.name: OnHover
examples.title: Revealed on hover
examples.description: The row appears on hover and on keyboard focus. On touch screens it is always visible.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Called when Copy is pressed, after copyValue reached the clipboard.

props.name: copyValue
props.description: Text the copy button writes to the clipboard.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Called when Try again is pressed. Shows the button.

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Called when Edit is pressed. Shows the button.

props.name: onRate
props.description: Called with the new rating. Pressing the active rating sends null.

props.name: visibility
props.description: hover reveals the row on hover and focus. It stays visible on touch screens.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations: toolbar, copy, copied, copyFailed, retry, edit, rateUp, rateDown.

props.name: children
props.description: Extra actions, placed after the built in ones.

accessibility: A toolbar with a label and a single tab stop. Arrow keys move between the buttons.
The rating buttons are toggle buttons that expose their pressed state. A pressed rating is filled as well as tinted.
Copying is confirmed with a polite announcement, and the button name changes to Copied for a moment.
With visibility set to hover the row still appears on keyboard focus and is always shown where there is no hover.
Arrow keys follow the reading direction in right to left layouts.

keyboard.description: Moves into and out of the toolbar.
Move between the actions.
Jump to the first or last action.
Activates the focused action.

do: Offer copy on every assistant message.
Keep the same order of actions on every message.
dont: Hide actions that people need on touch screens behind hover alone.

message-group.name: MessageGroup
message-group.summary: Consecutive messages from one author under a single avatar and name, so a long exchange stays easy to scan.
message-group.description: Wrap messages that follow each other from the same author in a MessageGroup. The name and avatar appear once, and each Message inside takes its role and author from the group.

examples.name: WithTimestamps
examples.title: Timestamps per message
examples.description: Each message keeps its own time.

props.name: author
props.description: Name shown once above the messages. It also names the group.

props.name: role
props.description: Who wrote the messages. Sets the side and the surface.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Avatar shown once beside the messages.

props.name: children
props.description: The Message elements of this author, oldest first.

accessibility: The group is named by its author.
Each message inside is still an article named by the author and its own time, so nothing is lost when reading message by message.
The avatar is decorative; the name carries the identity.

do: Start a new group when the author changes or after a long pause.
dont: Mix authors in one group.

message.name: Message
message.summary: One turn in a conversation from the user, the assistant or the system, with slots for an avatar, actions and a footer.
message.description: Use Message for each turn in a Thread. It lays out the author, time and content, and reflects the generation status you pass in. It does not fetch or stream anything itself: render the text you have, and set status as the response moves along.

examples.name: Status
examples.title: Submitted, streaming, stopped and failed
examples.description: The message is busy while submitted or streaming. Stopped and failed responses say so in words.

examples.name: Plain
examples.title: Plain variant with actions
examples.description: Plain lets long answers sit on the page without a bubble.

props.name: role
props.description: Who wrote the message. Inside a MessageGroup it defaults to the group role.

props.name: status
props.description: Generation status. submitted and streaming mark the message as busy.

props.name: author
props.description: Name of the author. Without it a default name is used for assistive technology only.

props.name: timestamp
props.description: When the message was sent, already formatted for display.

props.name: dateTime
props.description: Machine readable time for the time element, for example an ISO string.

props.name: actions
props.description: Slot under the content for a MessageActions row.

props.name: footer
props.description: Slot under the content for sources, attachments or a note.

props.name: variant
props.description: bubble wraps the content in a surface. plain lets it sit on the page.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations: user, assistant, system (default names), started, complete, stopped, error.

accessibility: Each message is an article named by its author and time.
While submitted or streaming the article is marked busy, so screen readers wait for the finished text.
Status changes are announced politely, once: started, finished, stopped, failed. Tokens are never announced.
Stopped and failed responses show a text label with an icon; the state never depends on colour alone.
User and assistant sides follow the reading direction, so right to left needs no extra props.

do: Pass status as the response progresses so assistive technology hears the changes.
Use plain for long assistant answers with headings, lists or code.
dont: Hide the author for sighted readers when several people share a conversation.
Put a streaming caret or loader in the status text; use StreamingText and ThinkingIndicator.

model-picker.name: ModelPicker
model-picker.summary: A compact select for choosing which model answers the next message, with a short description and capability badges on each option.
model-picker.description: Use ModelPicker when people can choose between models and the choice changes speed, depth or cost. Describe each model by what it is good for, in a few words. If there is only one model, or the product chooses for people, leave the picker out.

examples.name: Unavailable
examples.title: Unavailable models
examples.description: A disabled model stays in the list so people know it exists, with the reason in its description.

props.name: models
props.description: The models: { id, name, description?, badges?, disabled? }.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected model id, when controlled.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initially selected model id when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the id of the chosen model.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Keep the label for assistive technology only.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown when no model is selected.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Turns the picker off, for example while a response is streaming.

accessibility: Built on Select: a combobox that keeps focus on the trigger while arrow keys move through the list.
The label names the control even when it is visually hidden, and it can be translated.
Each option reads its name, badges and description together. Badges are text, never colour alone.
Disabled models are announced as unavailable and skipped by the arrow keys.
Typing a letter jumps to the model whose name starts with it.

keyboard.description: Opens the list.
Move through the models.
Chooses the active model and closes the list.
Closes the list without changing the model.

do: Describe models by what they are good for: “Quick answers”, “Long documents”.
Keep badges to one or two words each.
dont: List version numbers people have no way to compare.
Change the model in the middle of a response; apply it to the next message.

multi-select.name: MultiSelect
multi-select.summary: Choose several values; selections appear as removable tags and the list stays open while you pick.
multi-select.description: Use MultiSelect to choose any number of values from a list, such as the departments a signature template applies to. Selected values show as removable tags in the field. Turn on searchable for long lists. For fewer than six options consider a CheckboxGroup, which shows every choice at once.

examples.name: Searchable
examples.title: Searchable
examples.description: Type to filter; Backspace in an empty search removes the last tag.

props.name: options
props.description: Options or groups, as in Select.

props.name: searchable
props.description: Replace the button with a filter input.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder of the search input once values are selected.

props.name: showActions
props.description: Show “Select all” and a live count above the list.

props.name: name / form
props.description: Submits one hidden input per selected value.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: Accessible label for tag remove buttons (localisation).

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Shown when the search matches nothing.

accessibility: The control is a combobox controlling a listbox with aria-multiselectable="true"; options expose aria-selected.
Selected tags are a labelled list; each has a remove button with a descriptive label.
The “N selected” count is announced politely as selections change.
Choosing an option keeps the list open so several values can be picked in one pass.

keyboard.description: Open the list.
Move the active option.
Toggle the active option (Space only without search).
Select or deselect all visible options.
With an empty search, remove the last selected value.
Close the list.

do: Use searchable when there are more than about 15 options.
Show a count or summary when many values are selected.
dont: Use MultiSelect when only one value is allowed.
Hide important constraints, such as a maximum, until after submission.

native-select.name: NativeSelect
native-select.summary: A styled native <select> for simple choices and long lists.
native-select.description: NativeSelect keeps the operating system picker, which is the most usable option on phones and works without JavaScript. notification.name: Notification

NotificationList groups them, and NotificationCenter adds a header with an unread count, “Mark all as read”, an empty state and a footer. number-input.name: NumberInput
number-input.summary: Numeric entry with stepper buttons and full spinbutton keyboard support.

pagination.name: Pagination

password-input.name: PasswordInput
password-input.summary: Password entry with a show/hide toggle and an optional strength meter.
password-input.description: Use PasswordInput for sign-in and password creation. The visibility toggle lets people check what they typed, which reduces errors more than a confirm-password field. Enable strength on sign-up and password change; supply your own scorer to match your password policy.

pin-input.name: PinInput

popover.name: Popover
popover.summary: Non-modal floating content anchored to a trigger, for small forms, filters and details.
popover.description: Popover shows interactive content next to the element that opened it without blocking the rest of the page. progress-circle.name: ProgressCircle

progress.name: Progress

prompt-composer.name: PromptComposer
prompt-composer.summary: The message input for a conversation: a text area that grows as people type, with slots for attachments and tools, and a send button that becomes stop.

The target is at least 32px, and 44px on touch screens.

keyboard.description: Scrolls to the newest message.

do: Show an unread count when messages arrived while the reader was away.
dont: Show it while the reader is already at the newest message.

search-input.name: SearchInput
search-input.summary: A search field with a clear button, Escape to clear and an optional shortcut hint.
search-input.description: Use SearchInput to filter lists and tables or to start a search. It is a native search input (role searchbox) with a leading icon, a clear button once there is text, and a keyboard hint while empty. Pair with SearchableList or FilterBar for complete filtering patterns.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called when cleared by button or Escape.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Keyboard hint shown while empty, e.g. "⌘K".

props.name: loading
props.description: Replace the search icon with a spinner.

accessibility: Renders <input type="search">, exposed as a searchbox.
Provide a label with aria-label or FormField; the placeholder is not a label.
Clearing returns focus to the field so typing can continue.
Announce result counts near the results with a live region (for example "12 templates").

keyboard.description: Clears the value (when not empty).
Calls onSearch.

searchable-list.name: SearchableList
searchable-list.summary: A search field paired with a filtered list, with result counts announced as you type.
searchable-list.description: Use SearchableList to let people find items in a list of tens to hundreds, such as organisation users or signature templates. In selectable mode, the search field drives a listbox for picking one item, like assigning a template owner. For choosing a value inside a form field, prefer Combobox.

examples.name: Selectable
examples.title: Pick one item
examples.description: Arrow keys move through matches while focus stays in the search field.

examples.name: Fuzzy
examples.title: Fuzzy ranking
examples.description: matchMode="fuzzy" ranks prefix and word matches first and tolerates gaps.

props.name: getItemLabel
props.description: Text used for matching and as the option name.

props.name: searchLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the search field.

props.name: getItemKey
props.description: Stable key; also the selection key.

props.name: getItemKeywords
props.description: Extra searchable text, such as email or team.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom item content. state has active, selected and query.

props.name: matchMode
props.description: Contains keeps original order; fuzzy ranks matches.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Turns the list into a single-select listbox.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: Called when an item is selected.

props.name: isItemDisabled
props.description: Disabled items are skipped and cannot be selected.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Max list height before it scrolls.

In selectable mode the search field is a combobox that controls the listbox; aria-activedescendant tracks the active option while focus stays in the field.
Escape clears the search, as in SearchInput.
Disabled items stay visible and are announced as unavailable.

keyboard.description: Selectable: move the active option.
Selectable: first option.
Selectable: last option.
Selectable: select the active option.
Clear the search.

do: Include secondary text, such as email or team, in getItemKeywords.
Write an empty state that suggests what to try next.
dont: Use for thousands of items without virtualisation; combine with VirtualizedList.
Use as a form field picker; use Combobox.

select.name: Select
select.summary: Choose one value from a list, with typeahead, groups, disabled options and form submission.
select.description: Use Select when the user picks exactly one value from a known list of roughly 5 to 30 options. For long or searchable lists use Combobox; for several values use MultiSelect; for 2 to 4 visible choices consider RadioGroup. Select is a select-only combobox (WAI-ARIA APG): focus stays on the trigger and the active option is announced through aria-activedescendant. It integrates with FormField and submits through a hidden input.

props.name: options
props.description: Options `{ value, label, description?, icon?, disabled? }`, or groups `{ label, options }`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the user picks an option.

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name; a hidden input carries the value.

props.name: form
props.description: Associate with a form by id.

props.name: ...props
props.description: Native attributes for the trigger, e.g. aria-label when used without FormField.

accessibility: The trigger is a button with role="combobox", aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Inside FormField it is labelled by the visible label and described by the description and error.
Options use role="option" with aria-selected; groups use role="group" labelled by their heading.
Focus never leaves the trigger; the active option is conveyed through aria-activedescendant.
Disabled options expose aria-disabled and are skipped by arrow keys and typeahead.

keyboard.description: Open the list at the selected option.
Open at, or move to, the first or last option.
Move the active option.
Move by ten options.
Typeahead by label, whether open or closed.
Select the active option and close.
Select the active option and move on.
Close without changing the value.

do: Order options logically: alphabetically, by frequency, or by magnitude.
Use a placeholder that tells people what to choose.
dont: Use Select for fewer than three options; use RadioGroup or a Switch.
Use Select for long lists people need to search; use Combobox.

sensitive-content-gate.name: SensitiveContentGate
sensitive-content-gate.summary: Hides content behind a short notice until the reader chooses to see it, then moves focus to it.
sensitive-content-gate.description: Use SensitiveContentGate when a response may be upsetting or private: a graphic description, medical detail, personal data. The reader sees why it is hidden and decides. Until then the content is not in the page at all, so it cannot be read by sight, by screen reader or by search.

examples.name: NoHide
examples.title: Reveal once
examples.description: With allowHide off the content stays visible after it is shown.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: Keep the choice in your own state, for example to remember it per conversation.

props.name: description
props.description: Why the content is hidden, in a sentence.

props.name: onRevealedChange
props.description: Called when the reader shows or hides the content.

props.name: children
props.description: The content behind the gate. Not rendered until revealed.

props.name: allowHide
props.description: Offer a button to hide the content again.

props.name: icon
props.description: The notice icon. Pass null for none.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations for the show and hide buttons and the name of the revealed region.

accessibility: Hidden content is not rendered, so it is absent from the accessibility tree, not just blurred.
The notice is a group named by its title and described by its explanation.
On reveal, focus moves to the content, which is a labelled region. Hiding returns focus to the Show content button.
Focus only moves after the reader acts; a change made by the app never moves it.
The reveal animation is a short fade and is removed with reduced motion.

keyboard.description: On Show content: reveals and moves focus to the content.
On Hide content: hides it and returns focus.

do: Say plainly what kind of content is hidden so people can decide.
Gate only the part that needs it, not the whole response.
dont: Use it to hide content people need to complete a task.
Blur content with CSS instead; it would still be read aloud.

separator.name: Separator
separator.summary: A thin rule between groups in menus, toolbars and lists.
separator.description: Separator is a quiet one-pixel line. It is decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology. Set `decorative={false}` when it divides meaningful groups, for example in a toolbar. For section breaks in page content, use Divider.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Hide from assistive technology; false exposes role="separator".

accessibility: Decorative separators use role="none".
Semantic separators expose role="separator" and aria-orientation when vertical.

do: Use between groups of related actions.
dont: Use as a heading underline.

sheet.name: Sheet
sheet.summary: A bottom sheet for mobile-first flows, with a drag handle to dismiss.
sheet.description: Sheet rises from the bottom of the screen and can be dragged down to close, matching how people expect overlays to behave on phones. On tablets and desktops it centres at up to 640px wide. It is a modal dialog with the same focus and Escape handling as Dialog; dragging is an addition, never the only way to close.

examples.name: Heights
examples.title: Heights
examples.description: auto fits content (up to 90%), half and full are fixed.

examples.name: ActionList
examples.title: Action list
examples.description: A common mobile pattern for share or more-actions menus.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render your own Button as the trigger.

props.name: dismissThreshold
props.description: Drag distance that dismisses: px, or a fraction of the height when below 1. A quick flick also dismisses.

props.name: showClose / closeLabel
props.description: Close button; keep it so keyboard and switch users can close.

accessibility: A modal dialog named by SheetTitle; the drag handle is decorative (aria-hidden).
Dragging is an enhancement. Escape, the close button and the backdrop all close the sheet too (WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements).
Focus is trapped while open and restored on close.

keyboard.description: Cycle focus inside the sheet.
Closes the sheet.

do: Use for short, mobile-first tasks: sharing, quick actions, pickers.
Keep the close button visible.
dont: Put long forms in a sheet; use a page or Drawer.

shimmer-text.name: ShimmerText
shimmer-text.summary: Text with a slow light sweep for labels of work in progress, such as Searching the web.
shimmer-text.description: Use ShimmerText for a short label that names what the assistant is doing right now. The sweep says the work is still going on without a spinner. Turn it off when the step is done. For the answer itself use StreamingText.

examples.name: Steps
examples.title: Steps of a task
examples.description: Only the current step is active. Finished steps are plain text.

examples.name: Toggle
examples.title: Active and done
examples.description: Set active to false when the work ends.

props.name: children
props.description: The label, for example "Searching the web".

props.name: active
props.description: Runs the light sweep. Turn it off when the work is done.

accessibility: It is plain text to assistive technology. The sweep carries no meaning of its own.
With reduced motion, in the high contrast theme and in forced colours there is no sweep and the text is shown in a solid colour.
It does not announce anything. Put it inside a status, such as ThinkingIndicator, when the label should be read out.
The sweep follows the reading direction in right to left languages.

do: Keep the label short and say what is happening: Searching the web, Reading 3 files.
Show one active label at a time.
dont: Use it on long paragraphs or on text people need to read closely.

sidebar.name: Sidebar
sidebar.summary: Composable primitives for application sidebar navigation, with an icon-only collapsed mode.
sidebar.description: Sidebar provides the parts of a navigation sidebar (header, groups, items, footer and a collapse toggle) without positioning itself. Place it in your existing layout, fixed, sticky or in a grid, so product shells such as eSignify’s 18rem ↔ 5rem collapsing sidebar keep their structure. Use activeStyle="inverted" for a filled active item.

examples.name: Collapsible
examples.title: Collapsible (eSignify style)
examples.description: Inverted active item; the toggle switches between 18rem and 5rem, showing icons with titles.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Called when the toggle is used.

props.name: as
props.description: Root element; nav creates a navigation landmark.

props.name: icon
props.description: Shown in both states; required for a useful collapsed sidebar.

props.name: badge
props.description: Trailing count; becomes a dot when collapsed.

props.name: href
props.description: Renders a link. Without href it renders a button.

accessibility: The root is a named navigation landmark; each group is a list named by its heading.
Collapsed mode hides labels visually only, so every item keeps its accessible name; a title shows the label on hover.
The toggle reports aria-expanded and controls the sidebar; collapsible groups are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded.
The active item is not conveyed by colour alone: it has aria-current and, in high contrast, an outline.

keyboard.description: Moves through items, group headings and the toggle.
Follows an item or toggles a group / the sidebar.

do: Give every item an icon if the sidebar can collapse.
Persist the collapsed state per user.
dont: Put more than about ten items in one group.
Hide primary destinations inside collapsed groups by default.

signature-pad.name: SignaturePad
signature-pad.summary: Captures a hand-drawn signature with pointer, touch or stylus, with undo, clear and form submission.
signature-pad.description: Use SignaturePad where a person signs a document on screen. Strokes are stored as points, so the drawing survives resizes and follows the theme. Drawing is not possible for everyone: always offer a typed or uploaded signature beside it, as the first example shows.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Drawing pad
examples.description: Undo removes the last stroke; Clear removes everything.

examples.name: InAForm
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: With a name, the signature is submitted as an SVG string (or a PNG data URL with format="png").

examples.name: ImperativeHandle
examples.title: Exporting
examples.description: Use the ref to export SVG or PNG, or to clear the pad from your own buttons.

examples.name: ReadOnly
examples.title: Read-only
examples.description: Show a captured signature without allowing changes.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled strokes. Each stroke is an array of { x, y } points in CSS pixels.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when a stroke is finished, undone or cleared.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the drawing area.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the drawing area in px. The width fills the container.

props.name: name
props.description: Adds a hidden input so the signature is submitted with a form.

props.name: format
props.description: What the hidden input carries: an SVG string or a PNG data URL.

props.name: showActions
props.description: Show the Undo and Clear buttons.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents drawing and removes the pad from the tab order.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the signature without allowing changes.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the pad invalid. Set automatically inside an erroring FormField.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations for buttons, the hint, announcements and the description.

props.name: ref
props.description: clear(), undo(), isEmpty(), toDataURL(type?) and toSVG().

accessibility: Drawing needs fine pointer control, so it must never be the only way to sign. Offer typing a name or uploading an image alongside it (WCAG 2.5.1, 2.5.7).
The pad is exposed as an image whose name states whether a signature is present, for example “Signature: no signature yet”.
A description tells keyboard and screen-reader users to use the typed or uploaded alternative.
Capturing, undoing and clearing are announced through a polite live region.
Undo and Clear are real buttons; Backspace or Delete on the focused pad also removes the last stroke.
Ink uses the theme’s text colour, so it keeps full contrast in light, dark and high contrast.

keyboard.description: Moves focus to the pad, then to Undo and Clear.
Removes the last stroke while the pad is focused.

do: Offer Draw, Type and Upload together, and let the person choose.
State what signing means next to the action: “By signing, you agree to…”.
dont: Make a drawn signature the only way to complete a document.
Treat the drawing as proof of identity; that belongs to your product’s signing process.

skeleton.name: Skeleton
skeleton.summary: Placeholder shapes that hold the layout while content loads.
skeleton.description: Skeletons reduce layout shift and make loading feel shorter by previewing the shape of what is coming. Match their shapes to the real content. Skeletons are invisible to screen readers, so mark the loading container aria-busy and add a short status message.

props.name: lines
props.description: Number of text lines; the last is shorter.

accessibility: Skeletons are always aria-hidden.
Set aria-busy="true" on the region being loaded and include a visually hidden status, e.g. "Loading templates…".
The shimmer is disabled for people who prefer reduced motion.

do: Mirror the real layout closely.
dont: Show skeletons for operations shorter than about 300ms.

skip-link.name: SkipLink
skip-link.summary: Lets keyboard users jump past navigation to the main content.
skip-link.description: Place SkipLink as the first element in <body>. It stays hidden until it receives focus, then appears at the top-left corner. Activating it moves focus to the target, #main by default, so the next Tab continues inside the content.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Click into the preview and press Tab to reveal the link.

props.name: target
props.description: Id of the element to jump to, with or without #.

accessibility: Satisfies WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks.
Moves focus, not just scroll position, by giving the target tabindex="-1" when needed.
Becomes visible on focus with the standard focus ring.

keyboard.description: From the top of the page, reveals the link.
Moves focus to the main content.

do: Render it first in the document.
Give the target a stable id.
dont: Hide it with display: none; it must stay focusable.

slash-command-menu.name: SlashCommandMenu
slash-command-menu.summary: A list of commands that opens when a draft starts with a slash, filtered as people type and chosen without leaving the text area.
slash-command-menu.description: Use SlashCommandMenu to offer actions from the composer: summarise, translate, start again. It opens when the draft starts with a slash and filters by what follows. Your app decides when it opens and what a command does. For referencing files or people, use MentionPicker.

examples.name: InComposer
examples.title: Commands from a slash
examples.description: Type after the slash to filter, then press Enter to run a command.

props.name: commands
props.description: The commands: { id, name, description?, icon?, shortcut? }.

props.name: anchor
props.description: The focused element the list belongs to, normally the composer text area. The list is placed against it and reads keys from it.

props.name: query
props.description: The text typed after the trigger character.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen entry. Insert it or run it, then close the list.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with false on Escape or a press outside.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows the loading label instead of the entries.

props.name: filter
props.description: Filter by query on the name and description. Set false when the server filters.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the listbox, for aria-controls on the text area.

props.name: onActiveDescendantChange
props.description: Called with the id of the active option, for aria-activedescendant on the text area.

props.name: disablePortal
props.description: Render in place instead of in a portal.

accessibility: A listbox with an accessible name, following the same pattern as MentionPicker. Focus stays in the text area.
Point the text area at the menu with aria-controls and aria-activedescendant, using id and onActiveDescendantChange.
Each option reads its name, its description and its shortcut. Shortcut keys have spoken labels, so ⌘ is read as Command.
Escape closes only the menu and keeps the draft.
The active option has a visible highlight, with an added outline in high contrast and forced colours.

keyboard.description: Move the active option, wrapping at the ends.
Move to the first or last option.
Choose the active option.
Closes the list and keeps the draft.

do: Name commands with one plain verb and describe the result in a few words.
Keep the list short enough to scan; put the most used commands first.
dont: Offer a command only here; give important actions a visible control too.
Run a destructive command without asking first.

slider.name: Slider
slider.summary: Pick a single value from a range by dragging or with the keyboard.
slider.description: Use Slider when the exact value matters less than its position in a range, or when users benefit from immediate visual feedback, such as logo size or reminder frequency. When precise entry matters, pair it with a NumberInput or use NumberInput alone.

props.name: onValueCommit
props.description: Called once when a drag ends or a key is pressed.

props.name: marks
props.description: Tick marks with optional labels; true marks every step.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Value bubble on hover/drag, or always.

props.name: name
props.description: Submit with forms via a hidden input.

accessibility: Implements the WAI-ARIA slider pattern: the thumb has role="slider" with aria-valuenow, min, max, orientation and aria-valuetext.
Label it with FormField, aria-label or aria-labelledby; inside FormField the thumb is labelled and described automatically.
Use formatValue so screen readers hear units ("45%", "3 days"), not bare numbers.
The thumb has an enlarged invisible hit area for touch, and the track responds to taps anywhere.

keyboard.description: Increase by one step.
Decrease by one step.
Change by a large step.
Jump to the minimum or maximum.

sortable-list.name: SortableList
sortable-list.summary: A list people can reorder by dragging, with the keyboard, or with move buttons, announcing every change.
sortable-list.description: Use SortableList when the order of items matters and people set it themselves: approval steps, signature fields, pinned templates. Dragging is one of three ways to reorder; the keyboard and the optional Move up and Move down buttons do the same job without a drag.

examples.name: MoveButtons
examples.title: With move buttons
examples.description: A single-pointer alternative to dragging, recommended on touch screens.

examples.name: RichItems
examples.title: Rich items
examples.description: renderItem receives the item and its state, so rows can show anything.

props.description: The items in their current order.

props.name: getItemLabel
props.description: Plain-text name used for handle labels and announcements. Defaults to the id.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Renders the row content. State has index, dragging and disabled.

props.name: onReorder
props.type: (items: T[], move: { from: number; to: number }) => void
props.description: Called with the new order when an item is dropped or moved.

props.name: showMoveButtons
props.description: Show Move up and Move down buttons on each row.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations for handle names, instructions and announcements.

accessibility: Each row has a handle button named after its item, for example “Reorder Legal review”, with the keyboard instructions as its description.
Keyboard reordering follows the accessible drag-and-drop pattern: pick up, move, drop or cancel. Nothing is committed until the item is dropped.
Every step is announced: “Picked up Legal review, position 1 of 4”, “moved to position 3 of 4”, “Dropped”, “Cancelled”.
Move up and Move down buttons give a single-pointer alternative to dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).
Focus stays on the moved item’s handle, so people can keep adjusting.
The list is a real list, so screen readers report the number of items and each position.

keyboard.description: Picks up the focused item, or drops it in its new position.
Moves the picked-up item one position.
Moves the picked-up item to the start or end.
Cancels and returns the item to where it started.
Drops the item where it is and moves focus on.

Save the new order as soon as it changes, or make the Save action obvious.
dont: Use it for lists that sort themselves (by date or name); offer sorting instead.
Hide the handle until hover; touch and keyboard users would never find it.

source-list.name: SourceList
source-list.summary: The sources behind an answer, shown as a compact row of sites that expands to a full numbered list.
source-list.description: Put a SourceList under an answer so readers can see what it is based on. The inline variant takes one line and expands on request. The list variant shows every source with its snippet, for a side panel or a detail view.

examples.name: List
examples.title: Full list
examples.description: The list variant shows each source with its number, site and snippet.

examples.name: Folded
examples.title: A long list, folded
examples.description: max folds the rest away behind one control in either variant.

props.name: sources
props.description: The sources in citation order: { id, title, url?, domain?, favicon?, snippet? }.

props.name: variant
props.description: A compact row that expands, or full rows.

props.name: max
props.description: How many sources show before the rest are folded away.

props.name: onSourceOpen
props.description: Called when the reader opens a source.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called when the list expands or collapses.

props.description: Translations for the heading, the expand and collapse controls and the new tab text.

accessibility: The list is a group named by its visible heading.
The expand control is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, and focus stays on it when the list opens or closes.
Each compact chip is named by its site and the full title, so sources from the same site can be told apart.
The expanded view is an ordered list, so screen readers announce how many sources there are.
Chips and controls grow to 44px on touch screens.

keyboard.description: Moves through the sources and the expand control.
Opens the focused source.
On the control: expands or collapses the list.

do: Keep the same order and numbers as the citation markers in the answer.
Use the inline variant under a message and the list variant where there is room to read.
dont: List sources that were retrieved and not used.
Hide the list when there is only one source.

source-preview.name: SourcePreview
source-preview.summary: A card for one source behind an answer: its title, site, a short snippet and a link to open it.
source-preview.description: Use SourcePreview wherever a reader should be able to judge a source before opening it: inside a citation preview, in a list of sources, or beside an answer. It only shows what you pass in; it never fetches the page.

examples.name: Numbered
examples.title: With a citation number
examples.description: index shows the same number as the matching CitationChip.

examples.name: LocalFile
examples.title: A source without a link
examples.description: Without a url the title becomes a button when onOpen is set, so the app can open the file itself.

props.name: source
props.description: The source: { title, url?, domain?, favicon?, snippet? }.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Called when the reader opens the source.

props.name: index
props.description: A citation number shown before the site name.

props.name: snippetLines
props.description: Lines of snippet shown before it is cut.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translation for the hidden “opens in a new tab” text.

accessibility: The title is a real link, or a button when there is no url, so it works with the keyboard and announces what it does.
Links that open a new tab say so to screen readers.
The site icon is decorative and falls back to a globe when it is missing or fails to load.
The site name is derived from the url when domain is not given, so readers always see where a link leads.

keyboard.description: Moves to the title link.
Opens the source.

do: Pass the real page title and a snippet that supports the claim.
Use the same index as the citation marker in the text.
dont: Show a source the answer did not use.
Shorten the title so much that the page cannot be recognised.

spacer.name: Spacer
spacer.summary: Adds a fixed gap from the scale, or flexes to push siblings apart.
spacer.description: Spacer is an escape hatch for the rare case where a gap belongs to one spot rather than to a whole group. In a flex row it grows to fill the remaining space, which pushes later items to the far edge. Prefer the `gap` prop of Stack and Inline wherever you can.
accessibility: Spacer is aria-hidden and never focusable.

do: Use a flexible spacer to push a trailing action to the end of a toolbar.
dont: Chain spacers to build layouts; use Stack gap.

spinner.name: Spinner
spinner.summary: An indeterminate loading indicator with an accessible status label.
spinner.description: Use Spinner for short waits of unknown length, such as loading a list or saving. For longer operations with known progress use Progress, and for loading page structure use Skeleton. Buttons have a built-in `loading` state, so don’t put a Spinner inside a Button.

examples.name: WithText
examples.title: With text
examples.description: When visible text explains the wait, silence the spinner’s own label.

props.name: label
props.description: Status text announced; null when a parent announces state.

accessibility: Exposes role="status" with an accessible label by default.
Pass label={null} to hide it when nearby text already describes the wait.
Rotation slows down, rather than stopping, under prefers-reduced-motion, so it still reads as loading.

do: Explain what is loading if it takes more than a second.
dont: Show several spinners at once.

split-button.name: SplitButton
split-button.summary: A primary action joined to a menu of closely related alternatives.
split-button.description: Use SplitButton when one action is the clear default but a few variations are useful, such as “Deploy signatures” with “Schedule deployment”. The left half performs the default; the right half opens a DropdownMenu. If the actions are equally important, use a ButtonGroup or separate buttons instead.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: Accessible label of the menu toggle.

props.description: As Button, applied to the primary half (disabled applies to both).

accessibility: Both halves are native buttons inside a role="group"; the toggle has its own accessible label and aria-haspopup="menu".

do: Give the thread a height, for example by placing it in a flex column above the composer.
Pair it with ScrollToLatest so readers can return to the newest message.
dont: Scroll the thread yourself while a response streams; the thread already follows.
Put the composer inside the thread. Keep it below, outside the log.

time-picker.name: TimePicker
time-picker.summary: Enter a time of day with keyboard-friendly hour and minute segments.
time-picker.description: TimePicker uses separate spinbutton segments, the same model as the native time input: type digits (focus advances automatically) or use the arrow keys. The value is always 24-hour HH:MM (or HH:MM:SS) regardless of display, so it is easy to store and submit. The hour cycle follows the locale unless set.

examples.name: Step
examples.title: Quarter-hour steps
examples.description: Arrow keys move minutes in 15-minute increments.

props.description: Used to pick the default hour cycle.

props.name: name
props.description: Hidden input name for form submission.

accessibility: A group named by its FormField label, containing spinbuttons named Hours, Minutes (Seconds) and AM/PM.
Each spinbutton exposes aria-valuenow, min, max and a text value; empty segments announce “Empty”.
Each segment is a tab stop, matching native time inputs.

keyboard.description: Increment / decrement the segment (wraps).
Type a value; focus advances when the segment is complete.
Move between segments.
Minimum / maximum value.
Clear the segment.
Set AM / PM.

do: State the time zone in the description.
Use step for scheduling in fixed slots.
dont: Use for durations; use NumberInput.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: A chronological list of events, such as an audit trail or deployment history.
timeline.description: Use Timeline for event histories where order matters: contract audit trails, deployment logs and account activity. Each item has a time, title, optional description and a marker whose tone reflects status. Status is also given in text for screen readers.

examples.name: Alternate
examples.title: Alternating
examples.description: On screens 768px and wider, items alternate sides.

props.name: alternate
props.description: Alternate items left/right on wide screens.

props.description: Icon inside the marker; a dot otherwise.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Status announced to screen readers, e.g. "Failed".

accessibility: Renders an ordered list, so position and count are announced.
Times use <time datetime> for machine readability.
Markers are decorative. Pass statusLabel so status is never conveyed by colour alone.

do: Order newest first for activity feeds and oldest first for processes.
dont: Use Timeline for steps the user must complete; use Stepper.

toast.name: Toast
toast.summary: Brief, non-blocking messages about the result of an action, with optional Undo.
toast.description: Call toast() from anywhere after mounting a single <Toaster /> near your app root (these docs mount one for you). Toasts confirm outcomes such as “Template published” and offer quick follow-ups like Undo. They pause while hovered or focused, and toast.promise() tracks async work from loading to success or error. Use Alert for messages that must stay on the page, and ConfirmationDialog for decisions.

examples.name: Tones
examples.title: Tones

examples.name: WithAction

examples.description: Offer Undo instead of asking for confirmation.

props.name: id / dismissible / onDismiss

accessibility: Messages are announced through persistent live regions: polite for most tones, assertive for errors and warnings.
Timers pause while the pointer is over the toasts, while they contain focus, and while the tab is hidden (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable).
Press F8 to move focus to the toasts to reach actions with the keyboard.
Actions must also be available elsewhere; toasts disappear.

keyboard.description: Focus the toast list.
Move between toast actions and close buttons.

do: Confirm completed actions in a few words: “Template published”.
Offer Undo for reversible destructive actions.
dont: Use toasts for errors the user must fix in a form; show them inline.
Show more than one toast for one action.

toggle-button.name: ToggleButton
toggle-button.summary: A button that stays pressed, alone or in a group with single or multiple selection.
toggle-button.description: Use ToggleButton for a setting that switches on and off in place, like bold text or showing gridlines. ToggleButtonGroup arranges several toggles with one tab stop and arrow-key navigation: type="single" works like a segmented control (alignment, view mode) and type="multiple" allows any combination (text formatting). For settings that take effect as preferences, prefer Switch.

props.name: attached
props.description: Join buttons into a segmented bar.

accessibility: Each toggle exposes aria-pressed, so assistive technology announces "pressed" or "not pressed".
The group has one tab stop: Tab enters on the selected item and arrow keys move between items (roving tabindex).
Keep the label constant while toggling; the pressed state communicates the change, not a new label.

keyboard.description: Toggles the focused button.
Moves focus within a horizontal group.
Moves focus within a vertical group.
Moves to the first or last button.

do: Use icons with text, or provide aria-label on icon-only toggles.
dont: Change the button label when its state changes.

token-budget-meter.name: TokenBudgetMeter
token-budget-meter.summary: A compact meter of how much of the context or message limit is used, with a warning in words as the limit gets close.
token-budget-meter.description: Use TokenBudgetMeter in the footer of PromptComposer when a limit can stop people from sending, or when a long conversation is about to lose its earliest messages. Most people do not think in tokens: use format to speak in words, messages or a percentage where that is clearer.

props.name: used

props.name: limit
props.description: The size of the budget, in the same unit.

props.name: warnAt

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the value for display and for assistive technology. The default reads “1,200 of 8,000 tokens”.

props.name: variant
props.description: A small ring, a bar with the value, or the value as text.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show the formatted value beside the ring. The bar and text variants always show it.

accessibility: A meter with a name, a range and a value text that states the usage in words, including the warning.
The warning is an icon and text as well as a colour change, so it never depends on colour alone.
Reaching the warning threshold is announced politely once. It is announced again only after usage drops below the threshold and reaches it again.
Going over the limit is announced once as its own message.
With reduced motion the ring and bar change without animation. In forced colours they use system colours.

do: Say what happens at the limit, near the meter or in the warning label.
Use the text variant when space is tight and the number matters.
dont: Show a meter when there is no limit people can reach.
Rely on the ring alone to say a message is too long; block sending and explain why.

toolbar.name: Toolbar
toolbar.summary: Groups related controls into one tab stop with arrow-key navigation.
toolbar.description: Use Toolbar for clusters of frequently used controls that act on the same object, such as text formatting in the signature editor or bulk actions above a table. The whole toolbar is a single tab stop, and the arrow keys move between controls, which keeps keyboard navigation efficient on dense screens.

examples.name: WithInputs
examples.title: With a field and trailing actions
examples.description: Text fields keep Left and Right for the caret; Up and Down never apply in a horizontal toolbar.

props.description: Labels a cluster of related controls.

accessibility: Implements the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern: role="toolbar", aria-orientation and a roving tabindex.
Disabled controls are skipped by arrow keys.
Text fields inside the toolbar keep Left, Right, Home and End for editing.
Use ToggleButton for on/off formatting so aria-pressed communicates state.
Icon-only controls need labels; IconButton requires one.

keyboard.description: Moves focus into the toolbar (last focused control), then out of it.
Horizontal: previous or next control (wraps).
Vertical: previous or next control (wraps).
First or last control.

do: Group related controls and separate groups with ToolbarSeparator.
Keep the most used actions first.
dont: Put unrelated page navigation in a toolbar.
Overload a toolbar; move rare actions to a menu.

tooltip.name: Tooltip
tooltip.summary: A short text label that appears on hover and keyboard focus.
tooltip.description: Tooltips name icon-only controls and add brief, non-essential hints. They appear after a short delay on hover and immediately on keyboard focus, stay open while hovered, and close on Escape. Tooltip text must not be the only place important information lives, and it cannot contain links or buttons; use Popover or HoverCard for interactive content.

Opens on keyboard focus without a delay; opening by click focus is suppressed to avoid flicker.
Hoverable and dismissible without moving the pointer, meeting WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus.
Touch input never opens tooltips; do not rely on them for essential information.

keyboard.description: Focusing the trigger shows the tooltip.
Hides the tooltip.

do: Use to name icon-only buttons (in addition to their aria-label).
Keep text short and sentence-case.
dont: Put links, buttons or form fields in a tooltip.
Repeat the visible label of the trigger.

tree-view.name: TreeView
tree-view.summary: Displays and navigates hierarchical data with expandable branches.
tree-view.description: Use TreeView for nested structures people need to browse and pick from: teams in an organisation, folders, categories. It follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, including typeahead and expanding all siblings with *. Data is passed as items, and expansion and selection can be controlled.

examples.name: MultipleSelection
examples.title: Multiple selection
examples.description: Space toggles, Ctrl/⌘+A selects everything, Shift+arrows extends.

props.description: Called when branches open or close.

props.description: Icon per item using { expanded, selected, hasChildren, level }.

accessibility: tree, treeitem and group roles with aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset, aria-expanded and aria-selected.
One item is in the Tab order (roving tabindex); disabled items are skipped by arrow keys and announced as disabled.
aria-multiselectable is set in multiple selection mode.
Selection is shown with a tint and weight change plus an outline under forced colours.

First / last visible item.
Selects and activates the item.
Selects (toggles in multiple mode).
Expands all siblings of the focused item.
Moves to the next item starting with the typed characters.
Selects all (multiple mode).

do: Keep labels short and unique among siblings.
Show counts with meta rather than in the label.
dont: Use a tree for fewer than two levels; use a List.
Nest more than four or five levels deep.

virtualized-list.name: VirtualizedList
virtualized-list.summary: Renders very long lists efficiently by mounting only the visible window of items.
virtualized-list.description: Use VirtualizedList for thousands of items, such as audit logs, mailbox lists or recipients. Items can have a fixed height or be measured as they render. It can also act as a keyboard-selectable listbox. For short lists, a plain List is simpler and better for find-in-page.

props.description: Stable key per item; also the selection key.

The scroll container is focusable, so keyboard users can scroll a plain list with the arrow keys.
In listbox mode, focus stays on the container and aria-activedescendant points at the active option; the active option is scrolled into view.
Find-in-page cannot see unmounted items; pair long lists with SearchableList or a filter.

Provide a search or filter for long lists.
dont: Virtualise lists of a few dozen items.
Nest focusable controls in listbox options.

voice-input-button.name: VoiceInputButton
voice-input-button.summary: A microphone button for dictating a message, with idle, listening and processing states and a ring that follows the input level.
voice-input-button.description: Use VoiceInputButton in the trailing slot of PromptComposer. It shows what the microphone is doing and nothing more: your app asks for permission, records, and passes the state and level in. Show the unavailable state when the browser has no microphone or permission was refused.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Start and stop
examples.description: Press to listen, press again to finish. The level here is simulated.

props.name: level
props.description: Input level from 0 to 1, shown as a ring while listening.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Called when the button is pressed, to start or stop listening.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual weight while idle. Listening always uses the primary style.

props.name: labels
props.description: Translations: button, listening, processing, stopped and unavailable.

accessibility: A toggle button with aria-pressed. Its name stays “Voice input” in every state, so the pressed state is what changes.
Each change of state is announced politely once: Listening, Processing speech, Voice input stopped. The level is never announced.
Listening is shown by a filled button as well as the ring, so it does not depend on motion or colour alone.
With reduced motion the ring is steady instead of following the level.
When unavailable the button is disabled and its tooltip says why.
On touch screens the target grows to 44 pixels.

keyboard.description: Starts or stops listening.

do: Put what was heard into the composer so people can check it before sending.
Explain how to allow the microphone when it is unavailable.
dont: Start listening without a press.
Send the message as soon as speech ends; let people review it.
